One draft: drafting while its job runs, then valid, invalid, declined or failed, and confirmed or discarded after the owner's decision; the linked quick test's deterministic summary once it has a state. Read only. 404 assistant.draft_not_found

post.summary: The owner's confirm: re-validates the text sent, stores it as a normal library version and, when run is true, starts a quick test on the universe the owner picked. Needs a fresh password in the body and the switch allow_draft_confirm. 409 assistant.capability_off, assistant.draft_id_taken, assistant.draft_discarded; 422 assistant.draft_invalid, assistant.invalid, lab.invalid_strategy
The owner discards a draft (no password: the safe direction). A confirmed draft cannot be discarded. 409 assistant.draft_confirmed

get.summary: The newest stored briefing and weekly review texts (kind daily or weekly, limit 1 to 60, default 14), each with its source (model or deterministic), the reason a model text was not used, the guard's findings per attempt and the records behind the facts. Read only. 422 assistant.invalid

The stored briefing of a plan date (date=YYYY-MM-DD; default the newest stored one): the text, source, reason, word count, facts hash, model, attempts with findings and the evidence. Read only. 404 assistant.briefing_not_found; 422 assistant.invalid
The stored review text of an ISO week (week=YYYY-Www; default this week). Read only. 404 assistant.briefing_not_found; 422 assistant.invalid

The fixed-format text of a plan date or week (kind daily or weekly, subject a date or an ISO week, default the newest plan / this week), computed from the stored facts and shown. Writes nothing and never calls the model. 404 assistant.briefing_not_found; 409 assistant.briefing_not_evaluable (a week with no digest); 422 assistant.invalid

Whether the local model server is ready, loading, down or misconfigured, with the loaded model file (and its SHA-256 when it is a pinned one), the build and how to start it. Read only; cached a few seconds; no key, path or address in the answer

The assistant's settings in force (off by default), the model server, the tool server (not asked while the assistant is off), whether a turn is running, whether the nightly run blocks it, and the evaluation (not_yet_evaluated, passed or failed: from the accepted eval run, GET /api/assistant/evals/status). Read only

post.summary: Ask the assistant; the answer is a text/event-stream of turn, status, tool_call, tool_result, token, iteration_discard, ping, done and error events. Refusals come before the stream as problems: 409 assistant.disabled, assistant.busy, assistant.nightly_running; 503 assistant.model_unavailable (with state), assistant.tools_unavailable; 422 assistant.invalid, assistant.too_long; 404 assistant.not_found; 429 auth.rate_limited. Nothing is stored for a refusal

put.summary: Change the assistant's switches as the owner; appends one audited row and answers the status. Needs a session and the CSRF token. A change that only reduces exposure (assistant off, portfolio context off, a lower budget) needs no password; any change that turns something on or raises it needs the password in the body, checked on EVERY such change (an earlier step-up window does not count). 401 auth.invalid_credentials, 423 auth.locked, 403 assistant.owner_only, 400 assistant.values_invalid or assistant.reason_invalid, 409 assistant.stale, 429 auth.rate_limited

get.summary: The newest stored conversations (limit 1 to 50, default 20). Read only; nothing edits or deletes a conversation
One conversation: its messages in order, each assistant message with its tool-call summaries, the grounding status and the figures that were not found in the tool results. 404 assistant.not_found
One stored tool call with its arguments and the result envelope (up to 64 KB), as the audit keeps it. 404 assistant.not_found

The review of a plan: each primary and reserve ticket with its stored checklist per account (standing of every check, what needs the owner's confirmation, whether approve-all would take it), the cutoff and whether decisions are still open. Approved means watched; no order is placed and none exists. 404 plans.not_found

post.summary: Approve one ticket as the owner (session and CSRF token; the owner is the session, never the body). Every account's stored checklist must allow it; a check that is not a pass needs a confirmation naming its code, the account and a reason of 1 to 200 characters; the account gate can never be overridden. 'Approved for watching: no order is placed and none exists.' 409 plans.checklist_blocked, plans.closed (cutoff passed), plans.move_refused or plans.stale (already decided), 400 checklist.* (confirmation), 404

Lower the size of a ticket for accounts it is already sized for (only reductions; nothing else can be edited). The ticket becomes Modified, not approved: approving it re-validates the change and the checklist. Refused after the cutoff. 400 plans.modification_invalid, 409 plans.closed, plans.move_refused, plans.checklist_blocked, 404
Reject one ticket as the owner. Allowed after the cutoff time until the cutoff job has closed the plan. 409 plans.move_refused or plans.stale, 404

Approve every primary, still-proposed ticket whose stored checklist is complete with every check passed on every account; tickets with a failed, warned or unavailable check, reserve, modified and already decided tickets are skipped and listed with the reason, never approved despite a check. 409 plans.closed, 404

get.summary: The suggestions inbox of a plan with the owner's seen marks. Advice only; it changes nothing. 404 plans.not_found

post.summary: Mark a suggestion as seen (an insert-only row; repeating it changes nothing). 404 plans.suggestion_not_found

get.summary: The learned changes of settings (newest first) with the Auto switch, the weekly cap and what it has used, the allow-list, and for each change whether approving or undoing it needs the owner's password

post.summary: Apply a proposed change as the owner. A loosening needs the password in the body (403 auth.step_up_required without it, 401 auth.invalid_credentials, 423 auth.locked); a tightening needs only the session. 404 learned.not_found, 409 learned.wrong_state or learned.stale, 422-class learned.config_invalid when the whole configuration with it would be invalid
Set a proposed change aside as the owner (the safe direction: no password). 404 learned.not_found, 409 learned.wrong_state

Undo an applied change in one step. Undoing a tightening is a loosening: it needs the password in the body, at any Auto state. 404 learned.not_found, 409 learned.wrong_state or learned.stale, 403 auth.step_up_required

AcceptProposalRequest.description: The body of `POST /api/assistant/proposals/{id}/accept` (spec P9-08 AC 9): the owner's password for THIS accept. The actor is never in it.

AcceptSuggestionInput.description: Accepting a suggested dividend: optionally the holding it is for (one of the account's; none: unallocated) and a note. The amount and the date are the ledger entry's.

AccountDetail.description:
Everything about one account. Secret values and tokens are never part of it (only set / not set); the client id is masked. ApiKeyIssuedOn and
ApiKeyExpiresOn are the day the Dhan API key was generated and the first day it is no longer valid (12 months). TokenStatus repeats Connection.Status.

AccountEventView.description: One audit entry of an account.

AccountOverrides.description: Per-account replacements for values of the risk profile; null means "use the profile's value".

AccountPhaseReport.description: The verdict of one account with its numbers. DateOnly? AccountPhaseReport.FirstMetAt is the date the streak first reached the need (a later break does not rewrite it); string? AccountPhaseReport.LastBreak names the date and the reasons of the last broken session.

AccountResponse.description: What the owner may see about their own account (never the hash or the lockout state).

AccountSummary.description:
One row of the accounts list. Broker is "dhan"; MaskedClientId shows the first four and last two characters; Secrets lists the
secret fields with set / not set; ApiKeyExpiresOn is the first day the Dhan API key is no longer valid; TokenStatus repeats
Connection.Status (for the list's health dot).

ActionCounts.description: What the Action center counts for the scope (before the status filter): items by state, and for the open items by rule (all seven rules, zeros included) and by severity (high, medium, info). `NoPrice` counts open holdings without a usable price (no price-based rule can fire for them).

ActionDecisionView.description: The outcome of a decision: `State``open|snoozed|done`, `SnoozedUntil`, and the item as it is now (null when the id is not produced by a rule now, which only a reopen can still ask about).

ActionItem.description:
One Action-center item. `Id` is stable (`{rule}:{holdingId}`, or `sector_concentration:{accountId}:{12 hex}`) and safe in a URL path. `Rule` is one of `below_cost`, `large_gain`, `overweight`, `sector_concentration`,
`long_term_soon`, `lagging_nifty`, `not_in_basket`; `Severity``high|medium|info`; `HoldingId`, `InstrumentId` and `Symbol` are null for an account-level item (concentration) and `InstrumentId` for a holding that is not in the
master list. `Title` and `Detail` are plain sentences; `Numbers` the figures behind them; `Suggestions` the buttons that make sense (`open|set_alert|add_to_basket|snooze|done`). `State` is `open|snoozed|done`;
`SnoozedUntil` the India date a snoozed item shows again. Severity, text and numbers are recomputed on every read.

ActionList.description: The items of the status asked for, most important first, and the counts of the whole scope.

ActionNumbers.description: The figures that made an item fire; which ones are set depends on the rule, the others are null. below_cost, large_gain: `PnlPct`, `Pnl`, `Invested`, `Value`, `ThresholdPct` (the band reached: 10 or 20 / 25). overweight: `WeightPct` of the account's priced value, `ThresholdPct` (the limit), `Positions` (priced positions of the account), `Value`. sector_concentration: `Sector`, `SectorSharePct` of the account's priced value, `ThresholdPct`, `SectorValue`, `Positions` (in the sector), `LargestSymbol`, `LargestHoldingId` and `LargestValue` of the largest holding in it. long_term_soon: `Lots`, `PnlPct`. lagging_nifty: `HeldDays`, `XirrPct`, `BenchmarkXirrPct`, `GapPp` (holding minus benchmark, negative), `ThresholdPp`. not_in_basket: `Invested`, `Value` (null when unpriced).

ActionThresholds.description: The thresholds of the Action-center rules (ADR 0022, doc 15 §3): percentages are percent numbers (10 = 10 %). The defaults are the ones of the design; the owner edits them in Settings within the fixed ranges below.

ActionThresholdsInput.description: The thresholds to save: every value is required. `MinPositions`, `LagDays` and `LongTermWindowDays` must be whole numbers.

ActionThresholdsView.description: The thresholds in force with the documented defaults; `IsDefault` when they are the defaults; `UpdatedBy`/`UpdatedAt` null while none are stored.

ActionUnavailable.description: Rules that could not be evaluated: `Lagging` holdings held long enough for the lagging-Nifty rule but without a usable benchmark or XIRR.

ActivityRow.description: One line of the day's activity, newest first. string ActivityRow.Kind is an action-log kind or `alarm`, `halt`, `drill`, `mode_change`, `settings_change`; string ActivityRow.By is `auto`, `tap`, `system` or `owner`.

AddCorporateActionRequest.description:
A corporate action to add by hand (it is applied at once). `exDate``yyyy-MM-dd` (2000-01-01 to a year ahead); `kind` split|bonus; `numerator` and `denominator` whole numbers 1 to 100000
(a split 1:1 changes nothing and is refused); `note` at most 200 characters. `acknowledgeCsvAdjusted` true says the owner knows the loaded CSV files are adjusted up to `csvAdjustedThrough`
and wants an ex-date on or before it anyway (otherwise 409 `data.csv_already_adjusted`).

AddMembersInput.description: Instruments to add (1 to 500; repeats count once) with an optional note stored on each new membership.

AddMembersResult.description:
What an add did (counts of distinct instruments): `added` became members, `alreadyMembers` were members already, `newlyTracked` of the added
ones were not tracked and are now. `memberCount` = members now.

AdjustmentActionView.description: One applied action in the `adjustment` block of a bars read: the ex-date, kind, ratio and the factor of the action itself.

AdjustmentView.description:
What an adjusted read applied: `applied` is the number of applied actions that changed the bars returned (those with an ex-date after the oldest bar), `factor` the cumulative factor of the oldest bar
returned (the strongest; newer bars have a factor closer to 1) and `actions` those actions, oldest ex-date first.

AggregatePhase.description:
The aggregate phase of a data job (ADR 0016 §6): `Done` of `Total` are instruments. `Buckets` counts the bars written (new or changed),
by timeframe; `Full` is true when everything was rebuilt rather than the ranges touched by this job. Part of the API (the job's `aggregate` block).

AggregatesCheck.description: Aggregates against the 1-minute bars: every stored 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 1D, 1W and 1M bucket in the window recomputed independently and compared exactly (OHLC, volume, bar count).

AggregatesOverview.description: The derived timeframes: per timeframe, when they were last built and how many instruments have changes that are not aggregated yet.

state.description: The state of the proposal after this call (`applied`).

alreadyApplied.description: True when the proposal was applied before this call (nothing was changed now).

skippedCells.description: The cells that were no longer Paper or Active (already paused, retired or changed).

state.description: The state of the proposal after this call (`applied`).

alreadyApplied.description: True when the proposal was applied before this call (nothing was changed now).

demoted.description: True when this call moved the model from champion to challenger; false when it was not the champion any more.

previousChampionId.description: The champion this model replaced, or null.

previousQualifies.description: Whether the previous champion's latest evaluation satisfied the predicate without the switch when the proposal was written. It is NOT re-promoted: with or without it there is no champion now, and only the owner can name one.

kind.description: owner or auto; an automatic approval is never counted as the owner's.

skipped.description: The primary tickets left for the owner, with the reason.

reason.description: Why, 1 to 500 characters; a default sentence when omitted.

confirmations.description: The checks approved despite, per account.

ApproveTicketRequest.description: The body of an approval. Everything is optional; a ticket whose checks all passed needs no body. The actor comes from the signed-in session, never from here.

conversationId.description: An existing conversation, or null to start one.

AssistantChatRequest.description: The body of `POST /api/assistant/chat`: the question and, to continue a conversation, its id.

portfolioContext.description: The portfolio views show data to the tools.

maxToolCalls.description: The budget of tool calls per question, 1 to 12.

expectedSettingsId.description: The row the form was loaded at (0 when none was stored); a stale form is a 409.

password.description: The owner's password, for a change that raises exposure.

allowDraftConfirm.description: The owner may confirm a strategy draft (P9-07); absent means unchanged.

autoLabQuickTest.description: A valid draft of the dedicated drafting job may be queued for a quick test without a confirm (P9-07 D9); absent means unchanged.

allowProposalAccept.description: Used by P9-08; absent means unchanged.

autoAcceptHypothesis.description: Used by P9-08; absent means unchanged.

AssistantSettingsRequest.description: The body of `PUT /api/assistant/settings`. The actor is never in it (it comes from the session). Password is the owner's password for THIS change; it is needed when the change turns something on or raises it, and is not needed to switch something off or lower it.

AssistantStatusView.description: What `GET /api/assistant/status` answers (spec P9-03 AC 9). No key, address or path in it.

AttentionAction.description:
What the owner can do about an item (ADR 0027), at most two per item. `Kind``route`: `Target` is an in-app path with its query (`/accounts?account=…&tab=connection`) to navigate to. `Kind``command`: `Target` is an existing
endpoint as `METHOD /api/path` (`POST /api/accounts/{id}/sync/broker-history`), which the browser calls with its session and CSRF token like any other call of the app - no new surface.

AuditCount.description: A count under a key (source, category or outcome).

AuditEntryDetailView.description: One row with its detail fields (IP address and user agent for a sign-in row; confirm reason, modification and cutoff for an approval).

AuditEntryView.description: One row of the audit, redacted. ActorKind is owner, system, rule, cli, other or other_address (a sign-in address that is not the owner's; no address is shown then).

AuditKindView.description: A kind a store can hold, with its category, outcome and words.

AuditKindsView.description: Every kind per source, for the filter lists.

AuditPageView.description: A page of the merged audit. NextCursor is null at the end. Limits are sentences the screen must show.

AuditSourceState.description: What happened to one store in this request: `value` (rows read), `empty` (none; the reason says whether it was not asked for or had none) or `unavailable` (the read failed; the reason is a fixed code).

AuditSummaryView.description: Counts of the window; Total is every row of the window, before any filter other than the dates.

AuditWindowView.description: The days a response covers (India dates, inclusive).

AutoChainItemView.description: One service of the chain. `ResumedByAuto` is true when turning Auto ON resumed it (OFF pauses it again).

regime.description: The regime of the cell, `all regimes` for a cell that spans them.

dataAsOf.description: The date the cell statistics are as of.

AutoEvidenceView.description: The evidence figures as text; a missing figure reads `unavailable` and is never a pass.

AutoNightView.description: The newest nightly run: `no_run`, `published` or `failed_closed` (then no suggestions are shown and `Reason` says why).

AutoPreconditionView.description: One thing Auto needs. `Status` is `pass`, `fail` or `unavailable`; only `pass` lets Auto turn ON.

AutoRefreshView.description: The daily automatic refresh: whether it is on, at what India time, and when it runs next.

isSet.description: Whether a scope was ever set.

hash.description: The scope hash that plans carry, or null.

summary.description: `eligible` with no scope, else the counts in words.

AutoScopeView.description: The scope in force. With none set, `IsSet` is false and every eligible instrument is considered.

oneOf.description: Indicative levels as of the close of the session, or null.

why.description: For a ticket not suggested: which evidence is missing; otherwise null.

AutoSuggestionView.description: One suggestion: what, why and on what evidence.

planId.description: The plan the suggestions come from.

scopeHash.description: The scope hash stored on the plan, or null when it was built without a scope.

suggestions.description: Primary tickets with all required evidence.

notSuggested.description: Primary tickets missing required evidence, with why.

AutoSuggestionsView.description: What to look at for one session, with the basis and the words that no order is placed.

AutoView.description: The whole readout. `Complete` is true only when Auto is ON and every chain service is on; with Auto ON and a service paused it is false and `Note` names the service.

id.description: The row in force; null while nothing was ever stored (defaults, all OFF).

notice.description: No order is placed in any setting.

AutonomySettingsView.description: The settings in force, with the history newest first.

BackfillProbeAccepted.description: The answer of an acceptance: the row.

BackfillProbeAcceptedView.description: The acceptance of the probe result.

BackfillView.description: The backfill keys of the underlying by their latest state, or `unavailable` when the fetch log holds none.

epochId.description: The epoch, or null before the first capture.

counts.description: What counts and what is set apart.

fan.description: The fan; empty unless the band is a figure.

BacktestVsPaperView.description: The backtest-versus-paper report (spec P10-04, R14). Every figure is a state and a number only for a value or provisional figure.

BadBar.description: A bar that broke a row rule: its start and what is wrong with it.

BarRow.description: One bar. Times of the day timeframes (`1D 1W 1M`) are India midnight of the first day of the bucket. `bars` counts the 1-minute bars in it; `complete` says none was missing. `source` (1m only): csv · dhan.

BarsOverview.description:
The stored 1-minute bars: instruments with bars, the first bar and the last bar (the "last tick"), how many trading days (by the trading calendar: weekdays without the holidays, with the special sessions) the last bar is behind the last
closed session (`expectedSession`: 15:30 India time, or the end of a special session, has passed), `stale` (behind) and how many instruments are behind or still empty (tracked without bars).

members.description: Members as of the stated date.

buyAndHold.description: Mean price return in percent, equal weight, no rebalancing.

excluded.description: Members left out, each with its reason.

BasketBenchmarkView.description: The buy-and-hold of one basket with the instruments left out.

BasketBudgetView.description: The budget of one basket: its share of the total open risk limit, in percent.

BasketContextDay.description: One stored day of a basket's context. A figure that is not a number is null; `state` is value or insufficient; `membershipBasis` is point_in_time or single_snapshot (never presented as point in time).

BasketContextView.description: The newest stored rows of one basket (at most 400), newest first. Descriptive only: nothing here is a signal.

BasketFetchRun.description: What a fetch run did, one outcome per source it checked.

BasketHistory.description: The newest additions and removals of a basket, newest first.

BasketHistoryEntry.description: An addition (`kind` = added, `by` = who added it) or removal (`kind` = removed, `by` = who removed it) of an instrument. Only additions carry a note (the one given when adding); a removal has none.

BasketInput.description: Attributes of a basket (create and replace). Missing colour = the default; missing purpose = trading; blank description = none.

BasketMemberView.description:
One stay of an instrument in a basket: `validFrom` = when it was added, `validTo` = when it was removed (null while it is a member),
`position` = place among the members (0 first), `addedBy` = the owner's address.
In a system (portfolio) basket a member is the instrument of the bucket's holdings: `id` = the (first) holding, `validFrom` = when the holding was first seen,
`addedBy` = "portfolio", `quantity` = units held (summed over the bucket's holdings of it) and `accountName` = the account(s) holding it; both are null in a manual basket.

BasketMembers.description:
The members of a basket, in their order. `asOf` is null for the current members, otherwise the India date they are as of (members at the end of that
day; removed ones show their `validTo`). `total` counts the items. `membersKnownSince` is set for a stored system basket: before that date the first known members are shown.

BasketOrderInput.description: Every active basket exactly once, in the wanted order.

window.description: The window and where each end came from.

membersAsOf.description: The India date of the member list.

membershipBasis.description: `dated` (membership history exists) or `single_snapshot` (members as of one date, not as of each trading day; survivorship applies, ISS-22).

membershipFrom.description: The first date with membership history.

members.description: The members counted and the ones left out, named.

index.description: The index the basket is set against.

hold.description: The basket's buy-and-hold price return in percent (P8-07).

series.description: The daily series of the charts; the same numbers are in the tables.

risk.description: Volatility, drawdown, beta, tracking and capture.

indexDifference.description: The passive difference to the index; never a trading result and never called alpha (BK-07 review).

correlation.description: Average correlation, effective bets and the matrix.

holdOut.description: The median split of the strategy trades of this basket (m23).

relativeStrength.description: The relative strength returns (m8); the rank is on the ranking board.

BasketProfileView.description: The performance profile of one basket (BK-07, metrics m1b to m16, m23): its own prices against an index, with every figure a MetricView (a number only for a value) and the basis printed. Nothing here is a trading result and none is a forecast.

window.description: The window and where it came from.

index.description: The index the strengths are against.

rankWindow.description: Sessions of the relative strength return the ranks are on; null when fewer than two baskets have one.

rows.description: One per basket, in the order asked.

overlap.description: The Jaccard index of the member sets of each pair of baskets at the end of the window.

separated.description: False means "not separated": every gap is not larger than its standard error (indicative, pairwise, uncorrected; not a significance test).

BasketRankingView.description:
Baskets side by side (BK-07): the relative strength return of each over 21, 63, 126 and 252 sessions, its rank (1 = strongest) on `RankWindow` and the return over the annualised volatility. A basket with no value has no rank, only its state. No label "best":
when a pair of neighbours is within its noise, `Separated` is false and the screen shows no order.

BasketRiskBudgetChangeBody.description: The owner's change of one basket's risk budget: 1 to 100 percent of the total open risk limit, or null to remove it. The password is needed for every change. The actor is never taken from the body.

BasketRiskBudgetsView.description: The basket budgets in force (a basket with none has no budget) and their history, newest first (the latest 50).

BasketSettingChangeView.description: One change of a basket setting in the history.

BasketSettingsChangeBody.description: The owner change of the basket settings (BK-08). A value left out stays as it is; clearCap true turns the cluster cap off. The password is needed for every change. The actor is never taken from the body.

maxClusterRiskPct.description: `selection.max_cluster_risk_pct`, percent of capital; null is OFF.

version.description: The newest row id (0 when none).

oneOf.description: The newest change with direction loosen, or null when none was ever made.

BasketSettingsView.description: The basket settings in force with their history (newest first, the latest 50). With no row everything is OFF: the gate reads the tracked set's breadth and no cap on open risk per correlation cluster applies.

BasketSourceSummary.description: The state of a system basket's file (`reason` = the short reason of the newest rejected or failed fetch while the state is rejected or failed): `state` never · ok · stale · rejected · failed; `unmatched` = members of the last applied or checked list that are not in the instrument list ("N members not in your instrument list").

BasketSourceView.description: The source of a system basket and its last 20 fetches (no raw file). `enabled` = the owner has turned this file on; `unmatchedSymbols` = the symbols of the last checked list that are not in the instrument list (the "N members not in your instrument list").

BasketVersionDetail.description: One version with its scores, named exclusions (`universeSize = members + belowThreshold + excluded`) and the parameters it was computed with.

BasketVersionPage.description: The versions of a derived basket, newest first, with the definition they were formed by.

BasketVersionSummary.description: One version of a derived basket in the list (`outcome`: applied, not_formed; `provenance`: derived or recomputed).

BasketView.description:
A basket. `purpose`: trading · long_term · watch. `position` = place among the active baskets (0 first; the system baskets count on their own, in their group).
`memberCount` = instruments in it now. `archivedAt` is null for an active basket (archived ones are only listed on request).
`kind`: manual (the owner's) · portfolio (an account's portfolio bucket, ADR 0014); `system` = true for the latter: read-only, never archived, its members are the
bucket's current holdings. The stored system baskets (kind index, list, derived; BK-01) are read-only too: `membersKnownSince` = the first date their membership is known (earlier dates show the first known members, ISS-22), `source` = the state of their file.
`accountId`/`accountName` are set for the default bucket of an account.

days.description: The days compared (sessions on which every member has a close, from the first to the last exit of the out-of-sample trades).

members.description: The instruments of the run's universe.

strategySharpe.description: The daily Sharpe of the out-of-sample net R summed by exit day; null when not measured.

holdSharpe.description: The daily Sharpe of the equal-weight hold of the members over the same days; null when not measured.

reason.description: Why there is no comparison (too few days, a member left out, no variance, a failed read); empty when there is one.

basis.description: What is measured and what is not.

BenchmarkComparisonView.description:
The strategy against the buy-and-hold of the same universe over the same days (CF-11 row 13, ADR 0227), measured when a full Lab run ends and carried on its verdict. Report-only: nothing that judges the verdict reads it; only the readiness scorecard's row 13 does. It carries the two daily
Sharpe ratios, not a verdict: the row passes only when the strategy's is strictly greater (`BenchmarkComparison.Beats`). Null on the verdict of a run stored before it.

n.description: Distinct instruments included in a basket figure.

unavailableInputs.description: Inputs that do not exist, each with the reason.

oneOf.description: Only on a training benchmark (AU-14): that it is a training simulation, not evidence, and the range cut to the training window; absent from the evidence benchmarks.

BenchmarkEvidenceView.description: The evidence of a benchmark read: it has no runs or trades, so it states its basis, the instruments behind it, its range, its limits and what is unavailable.

BenchmarkExclusionView.description: An instrument left out; Reason is no_bars, too_few_bars, starts_late, ends_early, discontinuity or bad_price.

BenchmarkInput.description: Sets the benchmark: the id of a master-list index.

BenchmarkView.description: The benchmark in force (all null when the master list has no such index yet). `IsDefault`: the owner has not chosen one, Nifty 50 applies.

BenchmarkWindowView.description: The window. Each bound says where it came from, `query` or `runs` (the default run set); `Source` is `query` only when both did.

BillCandidate.description: A security a name may mean: `Isin`, `Symbol`, `Name` and — when it is a holding of the account or a share of the instrument master — `HoldingId` or `InstrumentId`.

BillCharges.description: The charges of the report's rows added up (`Total`, every row, whatever becomes of it) against the report's own total charges (`ReportTotal`; null when the report has none); `Matches` within ₹0.01.

BillCoverage.description: What the broker's own trades cover (ADR 0029): `Covered` trades of the report are left out because Dhan's trade history has the same day, ISIN and side; the days whose totals differ are listed (at most 50; `DifferencesTotal` counts all).

BillDetails.description: What is particular to a global transaction report: the names (every one that is a share or ETF, at most 500 listed; `NamesTotal` counts all) with what they mean, how many are unresolved, the coverage by the broker's trades and the charges check.

BillDifference.description: A day, security and side whose total quantity differs between the report's bill rows and the broker's own trades (the broker's win; shown, not hidden).

BillNameView.description:
A scrip name of a global transaction report. `Name` is the name as written (plain text, untrusted), `NameKey` the name reduced to what the server compares names by (key the choices by it), `SymbolHint` the ticker in brackets. `Status`: `resolved`,
`ambiguous` (more than one security fits: `Candidates`) or `needs_match` (none: its trades are kept without an ISIN). `Kind` is the rule that decided: `choice`, `alias`, `symbol`, `holding`, `master`, `learned` (a demat or depository file taught
it), `partial` (a spelling that differs by a word's ending: check it), `none`.

BlockerView.description: A service that would restart the count when it runs.

BlotterRow.description:
One order of the day. string BlotterRow.State is P12-01's word, passed through unchanged when it is not one of the fourteen (bool BlotterRow.StateKnown false). string BlotterRow.By is `tap`, `auto`, `system` or `owner`. Slippage is the fill's
price against the ticket price, positive when worse for the owner. string? BlotterRow.AlgoId is only what the broker returned.

BreachView.description: One breach rule that fires now (B1 to B7) or still holds a hold.

BreadthFigureView.description: One breadth share with the members behind it.

BriefingAttemptView.description: One model attempt, as the API shows it. The refused text itself stays in the audit table.

BriefingEvidenceView.description: The records behind the facts of a briefing.

BriefingFindingView.description: One finding of the guard, as the API shows it.

BriefingView.description: A briefing or weekly review text (spec P9-06 Contract). `Id` is null for a preview, which stores nothing. `Source` is `model` or `deterministic`; `Reason` is null for the model.

BrokerDroppedRow.description: Where one dropped row of a broker read lies, and why it was dropped: the dates of the request that returned it (DateOnly BrokerDroppedRow.WindowFrom, DateOnly BrokerDroppedRow.WindowTo; after a split, the half that was asked), the int BrokerDroppedRow.Page of the answer (0 for the ledger, which has one) and the zero-based int BrokerDroppedRow.RowIndex of the row in that answer, so the owner can look the row up in Dhan's own statement. Location and reason code only: never a name, symbol, amount, id or narration of the row (roadmap ISS-03).

BrokerHistoryInput.description: Optional body of "Sync now" for the broker history: the first date to read, instead of the watermark (or, for an account never read, the first import date).

BrokerHistoryRunView.description: The answer of "Sync now": the trades run and, when it succeeded and has been carried on to it, the ledger run. Started over the API, the answer holds the trades run as it begins (`running`); the status says how far both are.

BrokerHistoryStatusView.description: The status of the broker history sync of an account: whether a run is running, both kinds, the next scheduled run (null when the service is paused or there is none) and three figures that come from the latest succeeded trades run and from no other (nothing is carried forward from older runs, and a run that was skipped, failed or is still running does not change them): `HoldingsRebuilt` (rebuilt automatically by that run), `HoldingsNeedingReview` (a hand-dated lot; the owner uses the holding's rebuild preview) and `NeedsReviewSymbols`, the trading symbols of those holdings (at most 50, in the order the run listed them: alphabetical; `HoldingsNeedingReview` says how many there are in all). A quiet run that skipped the rebuild because nothing changed reports 0 rebuilt (holdings that need review are never skipped: every run looks at them again). `DeepenedTo` is the earliest date the nightly deepening of the trade history reached (null: it has not read an earlier year) and `DeepenExhausted` that it reads no more years (Dhan's history ends there, or the furthest year back is reached; ADR 0027).

BrokerIdView.description: The id a broker uses for the instrument (Dhan: security id + exchange segment).

droppedByReason.description: Why the latest run of this kind dropped rows (roadmap ISS-03): the number per reason code, the same figures as `LastRun.Counts.DroppedByReason`. Only the latest run counts: a later clean or skipped run shows none (empty when that run dropped none, or when there is no run, or it ran before the reasons were recorded). The codes are listed on `BrokerDropReasons`.

droppedRows.description: The place of the first five rows the latest run of this kind dropped (dates of the request, page, row index, reason code) - never the rows' content; a later clean or skipped run shows none. The same as `LastRun.Counts.DroppedRows`.

BrokerKindStatus.description:
How far one kind is read: the `Watermark` (last date read; null when nothing was read yet), the latest run and its windows done of total. The health (ADR 0027): `Attempts` is the number of the latest run within the day's occurrence (1 for the first, up to 4 with
the three quiet retries; 0 while there is no run), `ConsecutiveFailedDays` the days in a row whose last attempt failed (0 when the latest attempt succeeded), `LastFailureReason` a code (`unavailable`, `rate_limited`, `interrupted`, `rejected`,
`history_too_large`, `token_expired`, `token_refused`, `not_connected`, `data_changed`, `unexpected`; null while healthy) and `RetryAt` when the next quiet retry is due (null when none is pending). While a retry is pending the owner is told nothing. `DroppedByReason` and `DroppedRows` say why the latest run dropped rows (see below).

BrokerNotRebuilt.description:
A holding (or security) the automatic rebuild after a trade sync left alone, and why: `needs_review`, `quantity_mismatch`, `ambiguous`, `no_holding` or `changed_meanwhile`. The symbol is a ticker, never trade content.
`Detail` is the kind of mismatch for `quantity_mismatch` (`negative_opening`, `sell_exceeds_open`, `fractional_after_adjustment`: the first two are what an earlier read of the history can fix) and
`HoldingId` the single holding it is about (null for a security without one), so that a notice can open it.

droppedByReason.description: Why rows were dropped: the number of int BrokerSyncCounts.Dropped rows per reason code (`missing_id`, `bad_quantity`, `zero_amount` ...; see `BrokerDropReasons`). Empty in a run recorded before ISS-03 and when nothing was dropped; the figures add up to int BrokerSyncCounts.Dropped for a run that has them.

droppedRows.description: The location of the first int BrokerDrops.MaxLocations dropped rows of the run (request dates, page, row index and reason code) - never their content.

enriched.description: Trades stored already (counted in int BrokerSyncCounts.Duplicates too) that got an ISIN, charges or ticker they lacked from this read.

emptyByNoData.description: Windows (or half-windows) taken as empty only because Dhan answered DH-907 to the first page.

attempts.description: The number of this attempt within the occurrence: 1 for the first, up to 4 with the three retries. 0 for a run recorded before ADR 0027 (read as 1).

failureReason.description: The plain reason code of why the run failed; null while it runs and when it succeeded.

deepenedTo.description: The earliest date a read of earlier history reached in this run (null: none was made).

superseded.description: Trades run: bill-level rows of an imported Dhan report that the trades of this run replaced. Ledger run: imported depository-charge entries that the charges of this run replaced. Voided as superseded, ADR 0029.

supersededDiffering.description: Of the replaced rows' day-security-side groups, how many had a different total quantity than the broker's trades.

rereadVersion.description: The version of the Dhan mapping the windows in IReadOnlyList<BrokerWindowSpan> BrokerSyncCounts.RereadDone were read again with (0: none were read again). A failed run's list is only taken over by the run that follows it when the version is still the same (ADR 0030).

rereadDone.description:
The windows read again since the mapping changed (ADR 0027) that are done: each is added in the unit of work that stores the window, so a run that fails later does not make the retry read them again (ADR 0030). The run that follows a failed
one starts with the failed run's list (same int BrokerSyncCounts.RereadVersion) and adds its own. Dates only.

BrokerSyncCounts.description:
What a broker history run did (ADR 0025), kept as JSON on the run. int BrokerSyncCounts.WindowsDone of int BrokerSyncCounts.WindowsTotal date windows are read and stored; int BrokerSyncCounts.Halved windows were split in half because Dhan refused them as too large or answered "no data" for a stretch of several dates (the halves settle which).
int BrokerSyncCounts.Read rows came from Dhan, int BrokerSyncCounts.Stored are new, int BrokerSyncCounts.Duplicates were stored already, int BrokerSyncCounts.Dropped were unusable rows, int BrokerSyncCounts.Enriched of the int BrokerSyncCounts.Duplicates were completed (a trade stored by an earlier read without its ISIN or charges got them from this one; nothing else of it is touched) and int BrokerSyncCounts.Skipped were not NSE equity trades (by reason in
IReadOnlyDictionary<string, int> BrokerSyncCounts.SkippedByReason). After a trade run the automatic rebuild adds int BrokerSyncCounts.Rebuilt holdings rebuilt, int BrokerSyncCounts.Unchanged already right, int BrokerSyncCounts.NeedsReview holdings with a hand-dated lot that were left alone and the
first int BrokerSyncCounts.MaxNotRebuiltListed of the holdings or securities that were left alone with their reason (int BrokerSyncCounts.NotRebuiltTotal counts all of them). int BrokerSyncCounts.EmptyByNoData counts the windows (or half-windows) that were taken as
empty only because Dhan answered DH-907 ("incorrect parameters or no data present") to the first page: that code means both "nothing there" and "bad request", so the owner can see how often an empty stretch rested on it alone.
`Attempts` is the number of this attempt within the day's occurrence (1 for the scheduled or manual start, 2 to 4 for the quiet retries of ADR 0027), `FailureReason` the plain reason code of a failed run (`unavailable`, `rate_limited`,
`token_expired` ...) and `DeepenedTo` the earliest date an earlier-history read of this run reached. Counts only: no trade or ledger content.

BrokerSyncRunView.description:
A run that reads an account's trades or its ledger. `Kind``trades` or `ledger`; `Trigger``manual`, `scheduled` or `first` (the scheduled backfill of an account never read); `Status``running`,
`succeeded`, `failed` or `skipped`; `From` and `To` the dates it reads. `Counts` says what it did (windows done of total, rows read, new, already stored, unusable (`Counts.Dropped`, and `Counts.DroppedByReason`: how many per reason code, with `Counts.DroppedRows`: the place of the first five - request dates, page, row index and reason, never the row's content), skipped by reason; after a trade run the holdings
rebuilt, unchanged and needing review). `Error` is a short safe text.

BrokerWindowSpan.description: A stretch of whole India dates, DateOnly BrokerWindowSpan.From to DateOnly BrokerWindowSpan.To inclusive, that a run read again (IReadOnlyList<BrokerWindowSpan> BrokerSyncCounts.RereadDone). Dates only: no content of any row.

BucketInput.description: A new custom bucket. The name has 1 to 40 letters, digits, spaces, '_' or '-' and is unique ignoring case.

BucketView.description:
One bucket to pick from. IsAccountDefault is true for the automatic default bucket of an account that has the Portfolio role
(AccountId and AccountName name that account); custom buckets have neither.

BudgetChangeView.description: One change of a basket budget; BudgetPct null means the budget was removed.

CalendarDayView.description:
A date of the trading calendar (ADR 0017 §1). `kind`: holiday · special. A special session has `sessionFrom` and `sessionTo` (`HH:mm`, India time,
the end exclusive) and `minutes` (its length, the 1-minute bars a complete session has); a holiday has none of the three. `source`: manual · observed · nse.
`status`: confirmed · proposed (`dismissed` days are not listed). `replaces`: set only on a proposal that lies next to a confirmed day (a session seen on a listed
holiday, say) and names that day's kind: the confirmed day stays in force until the owner confirms the proposal (which replaces it) or dismisses it.

CalendarRefreshResult.description:
The answer of a refresh from NSE's public holiday list. It never fails the request: `succeeded` false means the list could not be fetched or read (`message` says why,
nothing changed). Otherwise the counts of the list's holidays that were added, updated, already known and left out (weekends, dates out of range, days the owner
decided or the stored bars contradict).

CalendarView.description:
The trading calendar. `days`: the confirmed holidays and special sessions from `from` to `to` (India dates, both included; default today and a
year on), by date. `proposals`: every proposed day, whatever its date, waiting for Confirm or Dismiss (including proposals that lie next to a confirmed day, marked `replaces`). `nextHoliday`: the first confirmed holiday
today or later (null when none is known).

score.description: The raw score of the trees.

CalibrationPoint.description: One point of the calibration table of a model: a raw score and the probability it maps to.

items.description: The whitelist in screen order, each with its state (OFF when it has no row).

history.description: The latest switches of all capabilities, newest first (at most 20).

CapabilitiesView.description: Every capability and the latest switches.

changed.description: True when a row was written; false when the log already said the same.

CapabilityChangeOutcome.description: What the switch did and what stands afterwards.

enabled.description: The newest row says on. False when there is no row.

changedAt.description: When the newest row was written; null when there is none.

reason.description: The reason of the newest row; null when there is none.

CaptureRunList.description: The capture runs with the label and the limits.

pending.description: Pairs left for a later run.

integrity.description: Stored entries a later replay disagreed with.

CaptureRunView.description: One session processed by a capture run.

tags.description: Every tag kind with its count (zeros included).

growingState.description: `evaluated` or `not_evaluable` (too few losses for two windows).

runKey.description: The 64-hex key of a stored run.

exit.description: The label of the exit policy the run used.

CellSource.description: A stored run whose closed trades make cells, with the labels the run does not carry itself: the style and the exit policy (the verb names them, as for an exit choice).

universe.description: The universe part of the key, `*` until BK-11.

expression.description: The expression part of the key, `cash` unless the key has an eighth part (P14-06).

state.description: The state after the last row (research without rows).

legalNext.description: The states it may move to.

problems.description: Rows that do not add up; empty when consistent.

note.description: What a reader must know: the state is a record; nothing acts on it before paper data and live exist.

CellStateView.description: Where a cell is, replayed from its changelog rows (P6-08).

independentN.description: CF-01 `IndependentN`: trades after same-session and serial correction; null when not computed. Three different numbers: double CellStatsView.EffectiveN is the recency-weight sum, `shrinkage.nUsed` (CF-02) is the smaller of this and the Kish weight n (sum w)^2 / sum w^2.

regimeName.description: The regime name of a regime cell (P6-02), null for a `*` cell.

regimeBasis.description: What the regime of the cell was built from: `index_and_vix` or `index_only`, or `all` for a `*` cell. A cell never mixes the two.

CellStatsView.description: One row of the cell statistics as the API shows it (P6-01), with the facts a reader needs to judge it (spec honest limits: the basis, the knobs, the evidence flag and the limits text).

CellView.description: One cell (timeframe and side) of a full test: the exit the walk-forward chose and how stable that choice was.

autoApproveTickets.description: The new value of `autonomy.auto_approve_tickets`: ON means tickets the rule allows need no manual approval, OFF means manual approval.

minPWin.description: The least lower-bound P(win), 0.5 to 0.99 (design default 0.58).

maxAutoPerDay.description: The most automatic approvals per planned session, 1 to 20.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS change. It is checked on every request (a step-up window opened earlier does not count and is not used up or extended); wrong ones count toward the sign-in lockout.

expectedSettingsId.description: Optional: the settings row the form was loaded at (0 when nothing was stored). When another change was made meanwhile the answer is 409 `autonomy.stale` and nothing is written; absent, the current row is read at submit as before.

ChangeAutonomyRequest.description: The body of the autonomy change. The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session.

enabled.description: True to switch the capability ON (it is off by default), false to switch it OFF.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS switch. Needed to switch ON and checked on every request (an earlier step-up window does not count and is not used up); not needed to switch OFF.

ChangeCapabilityRequest.description: The body of a capability switch. The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session.

on.description: True to allow the owner to confirm a sheet, false to stop allowing it. Switching it off does not revoke a confirmation.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS act.

ChangeChargeSheetCapabilityRequest.description: The body of the switch that allows confirming (off until the owner switches it on).

ChangeEssentialRequest.description: The body of a change to the Failure notices setting: on or off, and the password (needed to turn it OFF).

autoRampUp.description: live.auto_ramp_up (lets the evaluator raise S1 to S2 by rule when every gate passes; never above S2).

expectedSettingsId.description: The row the form was loaded at, 0 for none; a different row now is a 409.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS change.

ChangeLiveSettingsRequest.description: The body of a change of the live switches (spec P11-04). Both default OFF.

beforeRef.description: Reference to the thing before, or null.

afterRef.description: Reference to the thing after, or null.

ChangelogEntryView.description: A changelog row as the API shows it (P6-08): what changed, by whom, why, before and after, and the evidence. A revert has long? ChangelogEntryView.RevertsId.

ChangelogOutcome.description: What recording a transition or a revert wrote (P6-08).

changed.description: True when a row was written; false when the log already said the same.

ChargeSheetActOutcome.description: What the act did, and what stands afterwards.

sheetId.description: The sheet, for a confirmation or revoke.

ratesSha256.description: Its rates hash, for a confirmation or revoke.
The hash of its rates as confirmed.

ChargeSheetInForceView.description: The confirmation that is the newest act on the confirmation.

checked.description: What it was checked against; null means unchecked.

schedules.description: How many dated schedules it has.

ratesSha256.description: The SHA-256 of its rates now: what a confirmation must carry.

ChargeSheetPreviewView.description: A stored sheet as the owner is asked to confirm it.

capabilityOn.description: Whether the owner switched the capability to confirm on. OFF by default; nothing confirms while it is off.

state.description: `not_confirmed`, `confirmed`, `stale` (the stored sheet has other rates now), `sheet_missing` or `revoked`.

text.description: One sentence of what stands, as the reports will print it.

oneOf.description: The newest confirmation (confirmed, stale or missing), or null.
The stored sheet shown, or null.

sheetNote.description: Why there is no sheet to show, or null.

meaning.description: What confirming means, and what it does not.

ChargeSheetStatusView.description: What stands about the confirmation now (spec P8-23).

accountId.description: The account the confirmation is for.

codes.description: The check codes approved despite (never the account gate).

CheckConfirmationRequest.description: The owner's "approve despite" for one account: the check codes named and why. The ticket's own symbol is bound by the server; the owner is never part of any body.

CloneStrategyRequest.description: Body of the clone endpoint: the id of the new strategy; omitted keeps the id (a built-in gets `<ID>_COPY`).

ClonedStrategy.description: A clone (spec P5-01): the text with the new id, the hash of the version it came from (post it as `parentHash` to record the lineage) and the source.

rank.description: Percentile rank of the paper mean.

position.description: below, within or above; null when the band is not a figure.

CompareBandView.description: The backtest band of the mean.

paperN.description: Counted paper trades of the cell.

CompareCellView.description: One cell of the counted set against its reference.

id.description: The sheet id(s), or null when no counted trade was charged.

confirmedOn.description: The day the owner confirmed them; null when not confirmed.

CompareChargeSheetView.description: The charge sheet(s) of the counted trades and the owner's confirmation.

CompareCountsView.description: The counts of the epoch's tickets: what counts and what is set apart.

position.description: within or above; null when the reference is not a figure.

CompareDrawdownView.description: The backtest reference of the largest fall at the paper's trade count.

epochStart.description: The first session of the epoch.

snapshotKey.description: The cell snapshot in force at the start.

runKeys.description: The runs the reference was read from.

p05.description: 5th percentile of the draws' cumulative R.

CompareIntervalView.description: A 90% interval; each end is a figure.

maxDrawdownR.description: The largest fall of cumulative R in exit order.

CompareSensitivityView.description: The plan-price grades of all primary tickets of the epoch, beside the comparison and never used by it.

entriesKey.description: The key of the common entries.

members.description: The member runs, with the candidate each ran.

CompletenessCheck.description:
Completeness: the 1-minute bars the trading calendar expects in the window against the ones stored. `missingPercent` is of the expected minutes; `unfillableMinutes` are missing
minutes of sessions a refetch could not fill (a halt, a circuit-locked day): they are a warning, never a failure.

ComplianceLatest.description: The newest record of each kind; null = nothing recorded for that kind (empty, not "no change").

ComplianceRecordView.description: One stored record as the API shows it.

ComplianceView.description: The list (newest first), the latest per kind and whether the web may write now (the capability gate Live:Writes:Enabled).

truncated.description: True when the list was cut at the limit.

epochId.description: The epoch it led to or belongs to.

unexplained.description: True when there is no explanation and no owner note.

ConfigChangeView.description: One stored difference of the configuration.

rule.description: What a change of it does to the count.

ConfigComponentView.description: One component of the configuration with the rule that classes a change of it.

currentHash.description: The first 12 characters of the hash of the configuration now.

oneOf.description: The last full snapshot, or null.

blockers.description: Enabled services that restart the count.

unreadable.description: Groups that could not be read.

ConfigView.description: The configuration now, its class rules, the last snapshot and the differences not yet captured (spec P10-05 criteria 10 and 11a). A preview: nothing is stored.

sheetId.description: The stored sheet the owner confirms.

ratesSha256.description: The SHA-256 of its rates as the screen showed it; if the stored sheet has other rates now the answer is 409 `chargesheet.rates_changed`.

reason.description: Why, 1 to 500 characters (for example what the sheet was checked against).

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS act and checked on every request.

ConfirmChargeSheetRequest.description: The body of a confirmation of one stored charge sheet. The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session. There is no flag that says "confirmed": the body names the sheet and the rates hash the owner was shown.

ConfirmDraftRequest.description:
The body of `POST /api/assistant/strategy-drafts/{id}/confirm` (spec P9-07 AC 7): the owner's edited text (absent: the stored draft's), the universe of the quick test (a basket or symbols; the owner picks), whether to run it, and the owner's password for THIS confirm.
The actor is never in it.

ConfirmPromotionBody.description: The owner's confirmation: the password is checked afresh for this act.

ConfirmResultView.description: The answer to a tap or a skip. `AlreadyDecided` is true when an earlier request decided the ticket (the same decision, the same `DecidedAt`).

ConfirmTicketBody.description: The owner's tap: the hash of the text the card showed, the password when the ticket asks for it, and a reason when Soft checks did not pass. The actor is never taken from the body.

ConfirmTicketView.description:
One confirm ticket as the owner's card shows it (spec P12-08 Contract). `Text` is shown verbatim and never re-typed; `ServerNow` is the database clock at the read, so the countdown is the server's. `State` is
`open`, `confirmed`, `skipped`, `expired` or `refused` (a ticket past its expiry without an outcome reads `expired` before the loop writes it). `SoftCodes` lists the Soft checks not passed at issue: a
confirm then needs a reason.

ConnectStartView.description: Where to send the owner's browser to sign in at Dhan (same tab): Dhan's consent login page. The sign-in must come back before ExpiresAt.

ConnectionInput.description: New connection details of an account. Leave ClientId out to keep the current client id.

ConnectionView.description:
The account's connection to Dhan. Status is "not_connected", "connected", "expired" (the expiry has passed — derived when read,
no broker call needed). ExpiresAt is when the token stops working (as Dhan states, otherwise 24 hours after sign-in).
BrokerUserName and BrokerUserId (masked like the client id) are what Dhan reported for the token. LastError is a short safe text (at most
Dhan's error code). The token itself is never returned.

ContextBreadthView.description:
The breadth of the owner's tracked shares (P3-01e): `Latest` is the percent (0 to 100) of the latest day that has one, null when that day was `insufficient`; `State` is `value` or `insufficient` (null when no day has any);
`Voters`, `Universe` and `Excluded` are that day's counts; `PendingDays` are stored days still without a breadth (the last closed session can still gain bars); `InsufficientDates` names the thin days. The `Label` says what it is.

ContextCoverageView.description:
What the stored market context makes readable (`GET /api/data/context`, criterion 7). `Missing` names an unmet prerequisite (`index_not_tracked`, `vix_not_tracked`, `disabled`) with its `Fix`. `AgeSessions` is the number of
trading sessions the newest day is behind the last closed one; `Stale` is more than one.

ContextSkippedView.description: One day (or VIX leg) the derivation did not use, with the reason code and the bars it had.

ContributionRowView.description: One member's part of the hold return.

ConversationDetail.description: A conversation with its messages in order.

ConversationSummary.description: A line of the conversation list (newest first).

CorporateActionPage.description: A page of corporate actions, newest ex-date first. `pending` is the number of suggestions waiting for a decision over all instruments, whatever the filter.

CorporateActionView.description:
A split or bonus issue of an instrument (ADR 0017 §5). `kind`: split · bonus. `numerator:denominator` (`ratio`): for a split old shares : new shares (1:5 is one share into five), for a bonus
bonus shares : shares held (1:1 is one bonus share for each held). `factor` is the price multiplier for the bars before `exDate` (a 1:5 split 0.2, a 1:1 bonus 0.5). `status`: suggested
(found by the detection, changes nothing yet) · applied (adjusted reads use it) · ignored (declined, kept so it is not suggested again). `source`: manual · detected · csv.
`decidedAt` and `decidedBy` are set once the owner decided (not while suggested). `csvAdjustedThrough`: the date the instrument's loaded CSV files reach (their last bar, in India time; null when
none is loaded). Those files are already adjusted at source, so an action with an ex-date on or before it would adjust their prices twice.

CorrelationMatrixView.description: The matrix: `Total` members behind the figure, `Symbols` those drawn (at most 40, the most liquid, in sector order); a pair without enough common sessions is null.

CostBatchPage.description: One page of cost import batches, newest first.

CostBatchView.description: One import of a depository-charges sheet. `Status` is `imported` or `undone`; `ActiveEntries` counts its cost entries that are not voided; `Amount` is the rupees it stored.

CostImportResult.description: What an import of a depository-charges sheet did. `Batch` is null when nothing new was stored. `Imported` entries (`Amount` rupees) were stored; `AlreadyImported` and `AlreadyInLedger` lines were left out; `NamesLearned` names were remembered.

CostStressDelayView.description: The fill-one-minute-later test of CF-05, per signal: a signal that no longer fills counts as 0 R. The means and the share are null when the base is not above 0 (the reading then says not evaluable).

CostStressRowView.description: One row of the cost stress (CF-05): the multiplier, the out-of-sample trades restated, the mean stressed net R, the floor and its comparison, and the reading (`pass`, `fail` or `unavailable`, which is never a pass) with its reason.

trades.description: The out-of-sample trades judged (the sum of the four tier counts).

tierC.description: Trades in tier C (excluded from edge claims, counted here).

tierUnavailable.description: Trades with no usable 20-day median traded value (or whose bars could not be read).

capacityBreaches.description: Trades whose order is over a cap that was measured (the 20-day median share).

capacityUnavailable.description: Trades whose capacity could not be fully judged (the fill minute was not read, a traded value or the order value is missing, or the bars could not be read) and that are not already a breach.

settings.description: The text of the tier and capacity settings that produced the counts.

basis.description: What is measured and what is not read.

ordersOverEntryDayShare.description: Information only: orders over the capacity share of the entry day's traded value (about 375 times looser than the fill minute's); it can never make a pass. Null in a block produced before it.

minuteReads.description: Trades whose fill minute has a stored bar with a usable traded value (the 1 % cap was judged). Null in a block produced before the fill-minute read (S2b): that block has no judged minute cap and row 14 reads it as unavailable.

minuteUnavailable.description: Trades whose fill minute traded value was not read (int? CostStressTiersView.MinuteReads plus this is int CostStressTiersView.Trades). Null before S2b.

minuteReadLimit.description: The most trades of the run whose fill minute may be read (the setting at the time); trades beyond it are in int? CostStressTiersView.MinuteUnavailable. Null before S2b.

CostStressTiersView.description:
The liquidity tier and the capacity check of the out-of-sample trades of a Lab verdict (CF-05 D2 and D4, ADR 0223), the evidence of row 14 of the readiness scorecard. Report-only: nothing in the verdict reads it. Counts only; no trade is named.
A trade with no usable 20-day median is int CostStressTiersView.TierUnavailable. The capacity is held against 0.5 % of the 20-day median (measured on day bars) and 1 % of the fill minute's traded value (the stored minute bar of the fill minute, ADR 0224). A trade whose fill minute
could not be read (over the run's bound, a failed or timed-out read, no stored bar, no volume) has no complete capacity reading: int CostStressTiersView.CapacityUnavailable, never a pass. int? CostStressTiersView.OrdersOverEntryDayShare is information only.

mode.description: The mode when it was computed.

enforce.description: Whether a miss capped the outcome.

settings.description: The text of the settings that produced the figures.

costsChecked.description: The charge sheet is checked against a bill.

sheetId.description: The charge sheet the trades were costed with.

rows.description: 1x, the middle and the high multiplier.

tradable.description: The worst of the rows: `pass`, `fail` or `unavailable`.

oneOf.description: The delay test; null when the run did not take it (a full test, not a robust one).

capped.description: True when the outcome was capped at MARGINAL by an enforced stress gate.

limit.description: The first-order limit of the formula.

sheetRatesSha256.description: The hash of the sheet's rates the run was costed with, so a stored verdict says which numbers were checked.

oneOf.description: The liquidity tier and capacity counts of the trades (CF-05 follow-up, ADR 0223); null in a verdict stored before it ("produced before the tier and capacity check; re-run"). Nothing in the verdict reads it.

CostStressView.description:
The cost stress and the delay test of a Lab verdict (CF-05, ADR 0206), shown beside PASS/MARGINAL/FAIL: report-only unless the owner turns `Enforce` on, then a miss caps the outcome at MARGINAL and never raises it. Every settings figure used is in
string CostStressView.Settings and its hash in string CostStressView.SettingsHash. string CostStressView.Tradable is the worst of the three multipliers. bool CostStressView.CostsChecked is false until `cost-sheet check` has recorded a bill check, and the rows are then unavailable.

CostUndoResult.description: What undoing a cost batch did: its entries are voided (nothing is deleted). Undoing a batch again is a no-op (`AlreadyUndone`, `Voided` 0).

asOf.description: The last day of the data used.

sameRunsStored.description: How many stored counterfactuals use the same runs.

CounterfactualHeaderView.description: A stored counterfactual in a list (P8-12): the header only.

CounterfactualKnobsView.description: The knobs the result was made with.

gain.description: Mean paired log loss gain of retraining (positive: retraining was better).

gainStandardError.description: Standard error of the gain clustered by trade day; null with fewer than two days.

takeRUplift.description: Rows times the take-R difference, in R.

CounterfactualPooledView.description: Both sides pooled over some windows.

id.description: The row id; null inside the stored JSON (the row id is added on read).

cut.description: The day the frozen model stopped learning; null when no period could be made.

to.description: The last day of the data used.

frozenTrainRows.description: Rows the frozen model was fitted on.

oneOf.description: Both sides pooled over the judged windows.
Both sides pooled over every scored window.

limits.description: Sentences that must be shown with the result.

text.description: The printed text (also kept in the stored JSON; bounded: a handful of windows, one line each).

builtBy.description: Who built it; null inside the stored JSON.

createdAt.description: When it was stored; null inside the stored JSON.

sameRunsStored.description: How many stored counterfactuals use the same runs (every re-run is another trial); 0 inside the stored JSON.

CounterfactualReportView.description: The stored counterfactual as the API shows it (P8-12, `schemaVersion` 1): the view of the domain report, so NaN cannot enter the JSON. Every statistic is a server field; the screen computes none.

auc.description: Area under the ROC curve; null when one class is missing.

takeR.description: R per candidate of taking what the side scores at or above its own train base rate.

skippedMeanR.description: Mean R of the skipped trades; null when none.

CounterfactualSideView.description: One side of the counterfactual on a set of rows, as stored and shown (P8-12). A metric that cannot be computed is null, never NaN.

frozenTrainRows.description: Rows the frozen model was fitted on.

retrainedTrainRows.description: Rows the retrained model was fitted on.

informative.description: False: the same model on both sides, not judged.

gain.description: Paired log loss gain; null when not informative.

gainStandardError.description: Its standard error clustered by day.

takeRUplift.description: Take-R uplift of the window in R; null when not informative (a zero-width bar, never a bar of 0).

cumulativeTakeRUplift.description: The running total of the uplifts up to this window, in R.

note.description: A sentence for a window that is not judged, or null.

CreateAccountInput.description:
A new Dhan account. ClientId and Secrets (API key and secret) are required. ApiKeyIssuedOn is the day the API key was generated
(default today, India time).

CreateStrategyRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/lab/strategies`: the text, an optional note (at most 500 characters) and the hash of the version it was cloned from. There is no way to ask for a built-in: the request cannot set it.

CreatedStrategy.description: What a create did (spec P5-01): the version the content has, its hash and parent, and whether a row was written (false: the same content was already stored).

CrossingView.description: One stored crossing. `noticeId` is `crossing:{id}`; `state` is shown, snoozed or dismissed; `text` is built by the server and is plain text.

CsvFileCounts.description: The files by state over the whole folder (not narrowed by `state`, but by `q`), and how many cannot be loaded (`unmapped`: unknown, ambiguous or invalid name).

CsvFilePage.description: A page of the folder's files: changed and pending first, then loaded, by name; `total` is the number after the filters.

CsvFilePreview.description:
The dry run of the real reader over one file, nothing written. `verdict`: pass · refused · error (see `message`). `rows` are the data rows, `accepted` the ones that would be stored (`repaired` among them),
`rejected` the others, counted by reason in `rejections` with up to 10 `examples` (line numbers and reasons, never row values). `tradingDays` counts the distinct India dates of the accepted bars.
`wouldLoad`: passes and maps to exactly one instrument. `firstRows`: the first 5 accepted bars. `comparison` is null when the file does not pass or does not map.

CsvFileRow.description:
One file of the CSV folder. `state`: pending · loaded · changed (loaded, but size or modified time differ now). `symbol` is parsed from the name (null for an invalid name),
`mapping`: mapped · unknown · ambiguous · invalidName, `instrument` is set when mapped. `rows`, `firstBar`, `lastBar` (null for a file loaded before the range was recorded) and
`loadedAt` are set for loaded and changed files. `overlapsWith` (loaded and changed files; null for pending ones): the names of the other loaded files of the same instrument that cover part
of the same time — undoing either removes the instrument's CSV bars in the overlap, whichever file wrote them.

CsvInstrumentRef.description: The instrument a file maps to: its id and canonical symbol (`NSE:ABB`).

CsvOverview.description: The CSV folder: the files that match `<SYMBOL>_1m.csv[.gz]`, how many are loaded (unchanged since they were loaded) or pending, the rows loaded so far and when the last file was loaded.

CsvPhase.description:
The CSV phase of a data job (ADR 0016 §4): `Done` of `Total` are files. Rows are counted over all files read in this job. Part of the API
(the job's `csv` block) and stored with the job. `BarsRemoved` is set only by the job that undoes the load of one file (ADR 0017 §6): the CSV bars it removed (null for every other job).

CsvPreviewBar.description: An accepted bar, as the load would store it (after repair), with its start in India time.

CsvPreviewComparison.description:
What loading the file would do to the stored bars of its instrument, in bars: `wouldInsert` (minute not stored yet), `wouldUpdate` (a CSV bar of that minute with other values),
`keepExistingDhan` (a Dhan bar of that minute is kept: CSV never overwrites Dhan) and `unchanged` (same values). Counted over `comparedRows` accepted rows; when the file has more
accepted rows than the request may compare (`sampled`), a spread sample of whole batches is compared and the counts are of that sample, not scaled.

CsvPreviewResult.description: The previews in the order the files were asked for; `rowsRead` and `comparedRows` are the totals of the request (its limits are in the summary of the endpoint).

tickets.description: Tickets in the top K that day.

dayR.description: Sum of R of the day.

cumulativeR.description: Running sum up to and including the day.

CurvePoint.description: One plan-day of a top-K curve (P7-13).

DataAccountView.description: The primary Data account. `status`: connected · expired · notConnected.

DataInstrumentRow.description:
An instrument's coverage. `source`: csv · dhan · mixed (null without bars). `status`: current · behind · empty (tracked, no bars).
`daysBehind` counts trading days (null without bars). `openGaps`: sessions in the last weeks with missing bars that a refetch may still add.

DataJobView.description:
One data job (a run of the pipeline, ADR 0016). `status`: running · succeeded · failed · skipped (a scheduled run that did not start; `error` says why). `trigger`: manual · daily (the scheduled end-of-day run).
`refetchGaps`: the Dhan phase also retried the gaps it had given up on. `currentPhase` (while running): csv · dhan · aggregate · quality. `instrumentId` is set when the job is
about one instrument (a fix action of the Data quality screen). `csvFiles`: the files the CSV step was asked to load (null: every file of the folder). `undoCsvFile`: the file whose load this job undoes
(its `csv` block then reports `barsRemoved` and the message "CSV load of … undone, N bars removed"; the `aggregate` block rebuilds the instrument). `quality` is the data quality phase, present only when the job asked for the step (`runId` names its quality run).
Each phase block has `status` (notRequested · pending · running · succeeded · skipped · failed), `done` of `total` (files, instruments,
instruments), `message` and `code` (why it was skipped or failed) and its counts.

DataNotice.description:
Something about the data pipeline the owner should know, derived from the stored state like the account notices of the bell. `id` includes the situation (a new failed
run or a changed number of open gaps is a new notice, hence unread again). `kind`: data_gaps_open · data_quality_failed (instruments fail the data quality checks: warn within the allowed share, error when the gate blocks the nightly plan) · data_corporate_actions_pending (suggested splits or bonus issues wait for a decision; warn). `severity`: error · warn.

DataRoleInput.description: Switch the Data role. Kind ("primary" or "standby") is required when Enabled is true.

DataRoleView.description: Data role of an account: on/off and which kind.

DayUnlockBody.description: The owner's daily unlock of one account: a fresh password for this act.

DayUnlockView.description: The owner's unlock of one account for one India session date, valid until 15:30 India time.

alarm.description: Whether the last CUSUM event is an alarm.

events.description: How many alarms and clears the series has had.

latest.description: The latest event's evidence sentence, or null.

DecayCusumView.description: The P6-09 CUSUM on the same series, against the same reference.

limit.description: What it was judged against, or null.

trades.description: Trades the figure is based on.

proposalOnly.description: True for the CF-09 failure boundary.

DecayKillView.description: One kill rule's evaluation, with its numbers. An evaluation only: nothing is proposed, stored or executed in this part.

weak.description: Whether the mean is below the quarter floor.

DecayQuarterView.description: One calendar quarter of the by-quarter table.

state.description: `available` or `unavailable` (a series with no reference is never judged).

reason.description: Why it is unavailable, or null.

trades.description: Backtest trades the reference is made of (N_ref).

sigma.description: sigma, the sample standard deviation of the reference.

basis.description: `net` or `gross` of costs, as the backtest was run.

DecayReferenceView.description: The reference a series is judged against.

epoch.description: The paper epoch both series are read for; null when there is none.

hasSeries.description: Whether the strategy has any shadow edge candidate or any counted paper trade in the epoch (the endpoint answers 404 when it has neither).

reference.description: The reference, as the edge series sees it.

behavioural.description: The behavioural paper series, beside it.

kill.description: The kill rules evaluated on the edge series, proposals only (none is stored or executed).

DecayReportView.description:
The decay monitor of a strategy (spec CF-12 D1 and the kill-rule evaluations of D2, part 12a). The edge series (graded shadow trades that count for edge) is the primary reading and the P10 behavioural series sits beside it. Report only: no proposal is
written, nothing is paused and no order exists.

note.description: What the reader should know (no series, held back sessions, trades left out); null when nothing.

state.description: `no_series`, `unavailable` (no reference), `monitoring` (no completed window yet), `ok` or `alert` (the latest completed window is below its level). A flag; never a pass.

pendingTrades.description: Trades after the last completed window.

streak.description: Completed windows below their level in a row at the end.

twiceInARow.description: Whether the last two completed windows are both below.

firstTwiceAtWindow.description: The window at which two in a row was first reached, or null.

oneOf.description: The P6-09 CUSUM; null when the series is not judged.

weakQuarterShare.description: The share of quarters below the floor, or null.

DecaySeriesView.description: One series run through the decay monitor.
