sigmas.description: Standard errors below the reference mean.

rhoIsPlaceholder.description: Whether it is the placeholder until CF-01 estimates it.

DecaySettingsView.description: The settings that produced the figures.

designEffect.description: The mean design effect of its days (CF-01; the correlation is the placeholder until CF-01 estimates it).

threshold.description: The alert level for this window.

below.description: Whether the mean is below the level (an alert).

DecayWindowView.description: One completed window of the decay monitor.

mode.description: The mode when it was computed.

trials.description: N: the variants whose statistics are stored (the ledger count when the owner assumed the spread).

ledgerTrials.description: The variants the ledger counts for the family.

trialSrSd.description: sigma_SR: the standard deviation of the trial Sharpe ratios (or the owner's assumption).

luckBarSr.description: SR0: the Sharpe ratio luck alone is expected to reach among the trials.

sr.description: The judged variant's Sharpe ratio per trade (out-of-sample).

nEff.description: T: the trades the probability rests on (the effective trades unless the basis is raw).

minProbability.description: The level it is read against; it decides nothing in ReportOnly.

settings.description: The settings that produced the figure.

note.description: The reading and the honest limits, or the unavailable reason.

DeflatedSharpeView.description:
The deflated Sharpe ratio of the verdict (CF-03, ADR 0205), shown beside the heuristic factor and changing no outcome in `ReportOnly`. Per-trade units. Every figure is null when it could not be computed and string DeflatedSharpeView.Note then starts with
`unavailable:` and gives the reason; an unavailable figure is never a pass.

DematDifference.description: A security whose depository quantity differs from the synced holding's.

DematHeld.description: A security the depository holds that the account has no open holding for.

DematImportResult.description: What an import of a demat holding statement did: it changed no holding. `NamesLearned` names were remembered, `NamesKnown` were remembered already.

DematPreview.description: The preview of a demat holding statement: its securities, how many agree with the synced holdings, the quantity differences, the securities held at Dhan but not synced and the synced holdings missing from the statement (each list at most 200 long, the totals count all) and the names it teaches. Nothing here changes a holding. No notice is raised for these differences; they are shown here only.

DematSynced.description: An open holding of the account that the statement does not list.

mode.description: `Off`, `ReportOnly` or `Gate`, the mode when it was computed.

neededTrades.description: Independent trades needed to see the target edge (a lower bound: normal R).

minDetectableEdgeR.description: The smallest edge in R that NEff independent trades could see now.

minTrl.description: Minimum track record in iid trades.

minTrlDependent.description: MinTrl times the design effect: trades at this set's dependence.

yearsToEvidence.description: Years to reach NeededTrades at the arrival rate of NEff, if the rate and the edge hold.

enoughByNEff.description: Whether effective n reaches the minimum trades; null when unavailable.

note.description: Remarks and unavailable reasons.

summary.description: One line of words for a screen.

targetEdgeR.description: The edge in R that NeededTrades is about.

settings.description: The settings that produced the block (Lab verdicts); null for a stored cell row, whose snapshot key records them.

DependenceView.description:
How many independent trades a cell or a verdict rests on (CF-01, ADR 0203), as the API shows it. Every figure is null when it could not be computed and string DependenceView.Note then says `unavailable: <reason>`.
`IndependentN` (here double? DependenceView.NEff) is trades after same-session clustering and serial correction: not `EffectiveN` of a cell row (the recency-weight sum). Shown beside the old figures; it changes nothing unless the mode is `Gate`.

DepthRecorderSwitched.description: The answer of a switch change: the row and the new value.

DepthRecorderView.description:
The recorder as the owner sees it: the stored switch (`false` when never set), its history (newest first, the latest 50), the state word of the recorder's heartbeat (null when the feed host never reported) and the reasons it is not running now
(empty when all three gates are open and it is in its window or between windows). Nothing in it is depth data.

enabled.description: The new value of the owner's switch: ON allows the recorder to run (when the deployment flag and the service are on too), OFF stops it.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS change - ON or OFF. It is checked on every request (a step-up window opened earlier does not count and is not used up or extended); wrong ones count toward the sign-in lockout.

DepthSwitchRequest.description: The body of the depth-recorder switch. The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session.

DerivedBackfillInput.description: The body of a backfill request.

DerivedBasketOutcome.description: What one basket did in a run: `applied`, `unchanged` or `skipped` (with a reason).

DerivedDefinitionInfo.description:
What a derived basket is, from the catalogue: its name, the rule in one line, the one-line "what this basket is NOT" and the unit of its score
(`ratio` printed with 2 decimals, `percent` a share printed as "2.10 %", `rupees` printed in crore).

DerivedDefinitionView.description: The switch and parameters of a derived basket after an owner act.

DerivedParamsInput.description: The body of a parameter or switch change: new numbers (their overrides of the defaults, a whole new set) and/or the switch.

DerivedRun.description: The result of a refresh or backfill run.

DetectionResult.description: What a detection run did: `instruments` looked at, `candidates` found, `suggested` new suggestions stored (the others were known already, ignored ones included) and `pending` suggestions now waiting.

DhanOverview.description:
The Dhan Data API phase: the primary Data account (null when there is none), whether a fetch can run now (`canFetch`) and, when not, why
(`reason` in words, `reasonCode` data.dhan_not_available · data.dhan_not_connected), the settings, and the last successful fetch (time and bars added).

DhanPhase.description:
The Dhan phase of a data job (ADR 0016 §2, §7): `Done` of `Total` are instruments. `Bars` are the 1-minute bars Dhan returned;
`Rejected` are bars that did not lie on an IST minute inside a session or broke the row rules; `OverlapCompared` and
`OverlapMismatched` compare the overlap with the bars already stored (tolerance 0.05 %). `GapsFound` counts the instrument-sessions with missing bars
this phase planned to refetch or found still incomplete, `GapsFilled` those that now have all their bars and `GapsUnfillable` those a refetch added nothing to
(ADR 0017 §3). Part of the API (the job's `dhan` block).

DhanRedirectView.description: The redirect URL to register with the Dhan app, exactly as shown: `{PublicBaseUrl}/api/brokers/dhan/callback`.

DigestSection.description: One section of the weekly digest (P7-15). IReadOnlyList<string> DigestSection.Lines is never empty: a section with nothing to list says so.

id.description: The row id; null for a dry run that stored nothing.

createdAt.description: When it was stored; null for a dry run.

repeated.description: The week already had a digest: that one is shown and nothing was written.

DigestView.description: The weekly digest as the API and the verb show it.

primaryTickets.description: Primary tickets of the window (the seven categories add up to this).

closedTrades.description: Closed primary paper trades of the window, once per ticket.

DisciplineEvidenceView.description: What a discipline report rests on.

sumR.description: Sum of R of the graded tickets.

rMetric.description: Mean R: insufficient below 15 graded tickets, provisional below 30.

note.description: What is counted apart.

DisciplineLineView.description: One line of the discipline report on the wire.

amount.description: Rupees after the stored sheet's charges when charged.

DisciplineRupeesView.description: Rupees of one account on a discipline line.

epochId.description: The epoch; null when there is none yet.

from.description: The first day of the window.

to.description: The last day of the window.

lines.description: The lines in their fixed order.

unavailable.description: Why the report could not be built; null when it was.

DisciplineView.description: The discipline report of a window (spec P10-03, R19). Every R has its n and its state; there is no composite score.

alreadyDismissed.description: True when it was dismissed before this call (nothing was changed now; the first actor and reason stand).

reason.description: The reason given the first time.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS act. Missing: 403 auth.step_up_required; wrong: 401, counted toward the lockout.

DismissKillRequest.description: The body of a dismissal of a kill proposal. The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session.

lowerR.description: The lower edge; null for the open bin below the range.

upperR.description: The upper edge; null for the open bin above the range.

DistributionBinView.description: One bin of an R distribution: trades with R from LowerR (included) to UpperR (excluded); a null edge is open.

meanR.description: The mean R, or the reason there is no distribution.

bins.description: The bins in order, the open bin below first and the open bin above last.

DistributionGroupView.description: The R distribution of one group. The bins exist only when MetricView DistributionGroupView.MeanR is a value or provisional; otherwise it holds the reason there are none.

binWidthR.description: The width of a bin in R.

nonAdditive.description: A trade is in more than one group.

DistributionView.description: The R distributions of a report for a lens, one per group, with the evidence of the report.

DividendBadRow.description: A row that cannot be imported: the line of the file it starts on and why.

DividendBatchPage.description: One page of import batches, newest first.

DividendBatchView.description: One import of a dividend file. `Status` is `imported` or `undone`; `ActiveDividends` counts its dividends that are not voided; `Amount` is the rupees it stored.

DividendBeforeFirstLot.description: The dividends to be added that are dated before the account's first lot (`FirstLotDate`; null: the account has no lot): the net XIRR cannot count an inflow before the first outflow — read the earlier trade history.

DividendCandidate.description: A holding that fits an ambiguous scrip name.

DividendChoice.description:
What the owner decided for a scrip name of the file: exactly one of `HoldingId` (one of the account's holdings), `InstrumentId` (an NSE share or ETF of the instrument list) and `None` (keep the dividends unallocated). It applies to every
row with that name. `Name` is the scrip name as the file wrote it or the item's `NameKey` (best: send the `NameKey`); either way it is reduced to the key names are compared by (case, punctuation and company suffixes
ignored), so two spellings of one company are one scrip. Several choices for one scrip are fine when they agree (one is made of them) and a 400 when they disagree. With `Remember` the choice is saved as an alias, so later files with that name need no question.

DividendFileSummary.description:
What was in the file. `Rows` are the data rows (empty lines do not count), `Parsed` the valid rows (`ParsedAmount` their rupees), `Repeated` the valid rows that repeat an earlier row of the file identically (counted once; listed in
`IdenticalRepeats`, at most 200), `Distinct` the rows left (`Parsed - Repeated`). Of the distinct rows: `AlreadyImported` are stored already, `PossibleDuplicates` equal a dividend you typed in, and `ToAdd` would be stored,
among them `NeedsMatch` (no holding or instrument found: stored unallocated with the file's name) and `Ambiguous` (more than one holding fits: stored unallocated unless you choose). `Bad` lists the first 200 bad rows (line, reason);
`BadTotal` counts all of them.

DividendImportResult.description:
What an import did. `Batch` is null when nothing new was stored. `Imported` dividends (`Amount` rupees) were stored: `Allocated` to a holding, `InstrumentOnly` with an instrument but no holding, `Unallocated` with the
file's name only. `AlreadyImported` rows were stored before, `PossibleDuplicatesSkipped` equal a dividend you typed in and were not ticked, `AliasesSaved` names were remembered.

DividendInput.description:
A dividend typed in by the owner: for a holding (`HoldingId`; the account is then the holding's) or, left unallocated, for an account (`AccountId` alone). `PayDate` is the day the money was credited (not in the future),
`Amount` the rupees received (above 0, to the paisa), `PerShare` optional (above 0), `Note` optional plain text (at most 200 characters). The same account, holding, date and amount twice is allowed (two genuine payments) but the second asks
for a confirmation: `409 portfolio.possible_duplicate`, repeat with `Confirm` true.

DividendMatchView.description:
What a row's scrip name means. `Kind` is the rule that decided: `alias` (remembered), `isin`, `symbol` (the file's columns), `name` (equal names), `contains` (part of a name), `master` (a share of the instrument list that
is not held), `choice` (your pick in an import) or `none`. With a `HoldingId` the dividend belongs to that holding; with only an `InstrumentId` it keeps the instrument, ISIN and symbol but no holding; with neither it is
unallocated. `Candidates` (two or more) are the holdings an ambiguous name fits: nothing is guessed. `Symbol`, `Isin` and `Name` are those of the holding or instrument (plain text).

DividendPage.description: One page of dividends, newest first (pay date), voided ones included and flagged.

DividendPreviewItem.description:
A distinct row of the file. `Name` is the scrip name as the file wrote it (plain text, untrusted); `NameKey` is the name reduced to what the server compares names by (case, punctuation and company suffixes ignored,
the ampersand read as and): two spellings of one company have one `NameKey`, so group the rows that need a choice by it and key the choices by it. `Status`: `new`, `imported` (stored already), `possible_duplicate`, `needs_match`, `ambiguous`.
`Warnings`: `amount_mismatch` (per share × quantity differs from the amount paid by more than ₹0.01; the amount paid is used), `before_first_lot` (the date is before the account's first lot, so the net XIRR cannot count it),
`partial_name_match` (matched by part of the name: check it).

DividendPreviewReport.description:
The preview of a dividend file import — nothing is stored. `Format` is `dividends`. `Items` are the distinct rows in file order. `Digest` fingerprints what is shown; an import must send it back, and answers
`409 portfolio.preview_stale` when holdings, aliases or dividends changed since.

DividendRepeat.description: A payment that appears more than once, identically, in the file: counted once. `Lines` are the lines of its occurrences (at most 10 listed).

DividendSuggestionPage.description:
The suggested dividends of an account: its ledger entries of class `dividend` the owner has not accepted or dismissed, newest first. Dhan's documented ledger has no entry for an ordinary dividend, so the list is usually empty. The entries'
`Description` and `Narration` are Dhan's free text: untrusted, show as plain text.

DividendTotals.description: What an import would add: the number of dividends and rupees (the rows that are to be added — not stored yet, not possible duplicates) and the same by pay year.

DividendUndoResult.description: What undoing a batch did: its dividends are voided (nothing is deleted). Undoing a batch again is a no-op (`AlreadyUndone`, `Voided` 0).

DividendUploadForm.description: The multipart form of the dividend preview and import, for the API contract only (the request is read by DividendUploads). `AccountId` is the account, `File` the dividend list (CSV). For the import also `Digest` (required: the digest of the preview), `Choices` and `IncludeDuplicates`. A form field is text: send `Choices` and `IncludeDuplicates` as JSON text (`JSON.stringify` of a `DividendChoice[]` and of a list of line numbers of possible duplicates to import anyway); the types here say what the JSON holds.

DividendView.description:
A dividend. `HoldingId` is null for an unallocated one; `Symbol` and `Isin` are the holding's (or the matched instrument's) at the time. `Source` is `manual` or `csv` (read from a dividend file, ADR 0028). A dividend from a file
has its import's `BatchId`, the file's `Quantity` (shares) when it had one and, when it belongs to no holding, the file's `ScripName` (plain text, untrusted). A voided dividend does not count.

DividendYearTotal.description: Rows and rupees of one year.

DpCounts.description: The lines of a depository-charges sheet by what happens to them. `OffMarket` counts (among the others) the lines of type off-market.

DpLineView.description: A line of a depository-charges sheet. `Status`: `new` (stored by an import), `zero` (costs nothing), `buy_side` (not charged), `already_imported`, `already_in_ledger` (Dhan's ledger has a charge of that amount that day). `Side` is `buy`, `sell` or `other`.

DpPreview.description: The preview of a depository-charges sheet: the lines (at most 300 listed, `LinesTotal` counts all), their counts, the rupees an import would add to the account's costs and the names it teaches.

DraftAssumption.description: A value the model chose on its own: the YAML path (such as `exits[0].rr`), the value it wrote and why.

DraftConfirmed.description: What the owner's confirm made: the stored version, the quick test and whether the owner edited the text. `RunError` is the code of the refusal when a requested quick test could not start (the version is stored anyway).

DraftFinding.description: One thing a check found wrong with a draft: a code and the plain detail (a path or a number; never the idea text).

DraftNotExpressed.description: Something in the idea the strategy language cannot say today, with the reason; it keeps a number or time of the idea from being dropped silently.

DraftRequestedTest.description: The test the idea asked for, as text only. The owner picks the window and the universe at Confirm.

DraftRunSummary.description: The deterministic summary of the linked quick test (spec P9-07 AC 9): counts and the run's own labels, never a win rate, expectancy or verdict.

DraftView.description: A draft as the API serves it (spec P9-07 Contract).

Drawdown.description:
The largest peak-to-trough fall of a NAV series: `Pct` is a percent number (12.5 means it fell 12.5 %) from the peak on `From` to the low on `To`. A series that never falls (flat or rising)
gives 0 and no dates.

DrillRequestBody.description: Run drill for one account, with a fresh password. The actor is never taken from the body.

EntryWindowCellView.description: One cell of a stored entry-window study (P8-13b). A window is HH:mm text; a metric that cannot be computed is null. A status other than `Proposed` is the answer, shown as such.

EntryWindowKnobsView.description: The knobs an entry-window study was made with.

id.description: The row id; null inside the stored JSON.

outcome.description: `Proposed` when any cell has a proposed window, else `NoWindowProposed`.

from.description: Earliest trade date; null with no trades.

outsideSession.description: Trades outside the regular session (not bucketed).

limits.description: Sentences that must be shown with the result.

builtBy.description: Who stored it; null inside the stored JSON.

createdAt.description: When; null inside the stored JSON.

EntryWindowReportView.description: A stored entry-window study as the API shows it (`schemaVersion` 1). Every figure is a server field; the screen computes none.

EodOverview.description:
The scheduled end-of-day run (ADR 0017 §2) as set on the Services screen (ADR 0018): `enabled` (the service is not paused), `timeIst` (`HH:mm`, India time; empty when the schedule has no time of its own),
`nextRunAt` (the next scheduled start; null when paused or none ahead), `lastRun` (the latest automatic data job, null before the first) and `scheduleWords` (the schedule in words).

EodRunView.description:
An automatic (scheduled) run as the Data screen shows it. `status`: running · succeeded · failed · skipped; `message` is the reason a run failed or was skipped
(for example the Data account was not connected). `trigger` is always `daily` here.

truncated.description: True when the changes or notes were cut at the read limit of 200.

EpochDetail.description: One epoch with its changes and notes.

changeId.description: The change it explains, or null.

hypothesisId.description: The hypothesis it names, or null.

EpochNoteView.description: An owner's note on an epoch.

startedOn.description: The first session of the epoch.

endedOn.description: The next epoch's start, or null for the epoch in force.

fingerprint.description: The first 12 characters of the configuration hash, or null.

straddle.description: Entries set aside around a change (stored, shown, never counted).

riskDownChanges.description: Risk-down changes noted in the epoch.

unexplainedChanges.description: Changes with neither an explanation nor a note.

EpochView.description: One epoch as the API shows it (spec P10-05). Epochs are never pooled: each carries its own count.

date.description: The India date of the exits.

drawdownR.description: The running peak minus the running R.

trades.description: Trades that exited on the date.

EquityPointView.description: One point of an equity curve: the running R after the exits of a date and its fall from the running peak.

totalR.description: The final running R, or the reason there is no curve.

EquitySeriesView.description: The equity curve of one group. The points exist only when MetricView EquitySeriesView.TotalR is a value or provisional; a group below the minimum sample has no curve, so no flat line can be drawn for it.

nonAdditive.description: A trade is in more than one curve.

EquityView.description: The equity curves of a report for a lens, one per group, with the evidence of the report. At most int EquityView.MaxSeries groups are drawn; a lens with more is refused rather than cut silently.

EssentialSettingView.description: `Value` and `Default` are plain text (null when not known here); `IsDefault` is true when no row exists or it equals the default; `ChangedBy` and `ChangedAt` are null while never changed (or not recorded); `CanReset` and `ResetNote` say whether Reset to default works here.

EvalCaseView.description: One stored case repeat. The answer is fixture data only.

EvalDetailView.description: A run with its cases and the prompts and parameters it measured.

EvalRunView.description: A run as the API and the verb show it (spec P9-09 Contract). IsBaseline: the owner accepted it.

EvalStatusView.description:
The status of the evaluation (spec AC 10). Stale is true when the current fingerprint differs from the baseline's; Reasons names what differs. State feeds the assistant status:
`passed` only while a baseline exists and is not stale, `failed` when the newest gating run is not PASS, else `not_yet_evaluated`.

EvaluationView.description: The result of the assistant's evaluation (P9-09): `not_yet_evaluated` until that slice writes one.

EventFilterChangeBody.description: The owner's change of the event-risk filter. The password is needed for every change. The actor is never taken from the body.

EventFilterReasonView.description: Why the filter is not acting: `switch_off`, `history_unreadable`, `calendar_unreadable`, `no_calendar_rows`, or `no_entry_for_instruments` with the count of tracked instruments that have no visible results entry at all, and `no_upcoming_entry_for_instruments` with the count of those whose last meeting has passed and whose next is not yet intimated (unavailable too: fail closed, ADR 0182).

EventFilterRowView.description: One row of the decision history, newest first. string EventFilterRowView.SettingSnapshot is the JSON of the settings at that row.

EventFilterView.description:
The effective switch (the newest row; no row, or an unreadable history, is OFF), its settings, the latest 50 rows and the reasons the filter is not acting. int? EventFilterView.InstrumentsTracked and int? EventFilterView.InstrumentsWithEntry are the calendar coverage now
(null when the calendar could not be read). The auto option acts only on a hold-out confirmed KEEP: string EventFilterView.AutoVerdict is `unavailable`, a verdict word, or `KEEP_NOT_CONFIRMED` for a development KEEP that the hold-out has not confirmed.

EvidenceFigure.description: One figure of the evidence, built by the engine (P8-00 D1). Value is empty unless State is `value`: a figure that is insufficient or unavailable shows a word and no digit.

EvidenceView.description: The out-of-sample numbers a verdict was judged on. A number that is not finite (an infinite profit factor) is null; the reason of its gate says it in words.

ExclusionCountView.description: How many tickets were left out of the report for one reason.

ExecMetric.description:
A figure of the execution screens (spec P12-10 Contract, P8-00 D3). string ExecMetric.State is `value`, `insufficient`, `unavailable`, `not_evaluable` or `empty`; a digit exists only for `value`. An input that cannot be read is
`unavailable` with its string? ExecMetric.Reason, never zero. decimal? ExecMetric.Cap is the limit in force (null when the sheet leaves it unset, with the reason `cap_unset`).

ExecutionAlarmView.description: One alarm. Severity is `info`, `warn` or `critical`; the intent is null for an alarm about no single intent; ClearedAt and ClearedBy are null while the alarm is open.

ExecutionBreakResolution.description: The owner's answer to a break: `accept_broker` (adopt the broker's figure as true) or `dismiss_foreign` (a foreign item, remembered as explained for the day). The note is the owner's own text, at most 300 characters.

ExecutionBreakView.description: One break of a reconciliation run with its resolution, if any. Kind is one of the eight of spec P12-06.

ExecutionDayStateView.description: The state recorded at 09:10:30 India time for one session. Late means the service was not running then; the state is then `unavailable`.

ExecutionDrillRequestView.description:
One drill the owner asked for: the command row and, once the execution service carried it out, its answer. string? ExecutionDrillRequestView.Result is `done` or `refused`; string? ExecutionDrillRequestView.Code is `execution.drill_passed`, `execution.drill_failed`,
`execution.drill_refused:<why>` or `execution.drill_unavailable` (the service runs no drill outside the sandbox). Both null while the service has not answered.

ExecutionDrillStarted.description: The command row left for the execution service; the drill row appears when the service has run it (read the drills to see it).

ExecutionDrillView.description: One stored drill (spec P12-05 criterion 10): passed, how long the halt took to be seen in milliseconds, and the detail of what was proved. No order was sent in any case.

ExecutionDrillsView.description: The drills newest first (at most 50), the latest 20 requests with their answers, the age after which the mode ladder no longer counts a drill (int ExecutionDrillsView.MaxAgeDays) and the database clock.

ExecutionGapView.description: The execution gap by group, a total that is built from the same tickets, and the evidence.

ExecutionHaltEnd.description: How a halt ended: by the owner (release) or automatically (a clear of a code that may clear itself). The release reason is the owner's own text; the automatic clear carries none.

ExecutionHaltStarted.description: The command row left for the execution service; the halt itself is recorded when xd-exec carries it out (read the halts to see it).

ExecutionHaltView.description: One halt. Scope is `system` or `account`; level is `entries`, `cancel`, `exit_all` or `freeze`; End is null while it is active.

ExecutionIpAttestationView.description: The owner's claim, from Dhan's web tool, that orders are allowed for the address. A claim, not a verification (spec D5).

ExecutionModeAccountView.description: One account: its configured and effective mode, a change that waits for the next open, the open request, the next step of the ladder (null where there is none) and the latest 20 trail rows.

ExecutionModesView.description: bool? ExecutionModesView.ExecutionEnabled is null when the switch could not be read (it then counts as OFF).

ExecutionNotice.description: An item for the bell, in the shape of the portfolio notices. The id includes the cause, so a changed situation is a new item. A resolved item stays 24 hours and is not counted.

ExecutionOverview.description: bool? ExecutionOverview.CanaryPending is `exec.canary_pending` (null when it could not be read). IReadOnlyList<string> ExecutionOverview.Limits is the evidence line: what the numbers are and are not.

ExecutionPhaseReport.description: The report (spec P12-12 Contract). string ExecutionPhaseReport.ExitVerdict is the bare word, string ExecutionPhaseReport.ExitCriterion the labelled line; PhaseFact ExecutionPhaseReport.Boundary is a printed fact that does not change a streak.

ExecutionReadinessAccount.description:
One account's readiness: `State` is `ready`, `not_ready` or `unavailable` (also when no check was ever recorded: nothing is ready until it says so). ReadyAt is the start of the current unbroken run of ready checks of the session. IpModifyAfter is the first day the
IP can be changed at Dhan again. SendsPerSecondMax is the highest number of order sends within one second recorded in `broker_calls` for the date, or null when there is none.

ExecutionReadinessCheck.description: One check of the readiness verdict. Outcome is `pass`, `fail` or `unavailable`; only `pass` is ever shown as good. The text never holds a token, a client id or an address.

ExecutionRecheckView.description: The newest SEBI re-check of P11-05, read only.

ExecutionReconRunView.description: One reconciliation run. A run that could not read the broker is `Readable` false and carries a break: it is never clean.

id.description: plan, slippage, charges, net, missed_triggers or real_slippage.

ExecutionRowView.description: One row of the paper execution waterfall on the wire.

state.description: `recovering`, `ready`, `halted` or `down` (no heartbeat, or one older than 30 seconds).

lastBeatAt.description: The last heartbeat, null when there never was one.

ExecutionSettingsChangeBody.description: The owner's change of the global switches. The password is needed for every change; autoLiveEnabled true is always refused. The actor is never taken from the body.

ExecutionSettingsRowView.description: One stored snapshot of the global execution switches (spec P12-07 criterion 13, ADR 0174). The `values` object is not shown: this route does not change it.

ExecutionSettingsView.description:
The two global switches: the row in force (null: never written, both OFF), the raise waiting for its `effectiveFrom` (null: none), the latest 20 rows, and bool ExecutionSettingsView.AutoLiveLocked (always true: no route turns `auto_live_enabled`
on in this build). DateTimeOffset ExecutionSettingsView.ServerNow is the database clock.

service.description: The service as the heartbeat shows it.

environment.description: The service's process environment from its heartbeat: `none`, `sandbox` or `live`; `none` when it never reported.

accounts.description: Every account with its stored mode and its gate. The gate is closed for all of them until the mode ladder exists (P12-07).

halts.description: The halts in force. Always empty in this slice (the halt store comes with P12-05) and EntriesBlocked says so.

openIntents.description: Intents not yet in a final state.

settingsHash.description: Hash of the settings in force as the service reports it, null when it never reported.

entriesBlocked.description: True while no entry may leave: always true in this slice (recovery and the halt store do not exist yet).

anyAutomated.description: True while execution is enabled and an account's mode sends orders without the owner typing them (semi_auto or auto_live). No account can be there today.

killSwitchActive.description: True while any halt is in force (spec P12-10).

pollSeconds.description: How often the bell asks for notices: 5 while something is automated and the market is open, else 60.

marketOpen.description: True inside today's session in India time.

ExecutionView.description: How a service is run: retries (0–5 after a failed attempt), the timeout of an attempt in minutes (1–240), whether a missed run is made up for when the application starts, and whether a failure raises a notice in the bell.

comparisonKey.description: The comparison it was made from.

regime.description: The cell's regime (* until a regime exists).

defaultCandidateId.description: The exit used when no choice stands.

chosenCandidateId.description: The walk-forward choice; null when there is none.

noChoiceReason.description: Why there is none; null when there is one.

stable.description: True, false, or null for no statement.

agreeingFolds.description: Of those, folds agreeing with the modal winner.

positiveFolds.description: Of the agreeing, folds positive out of sample.

chancePass.description: Exact probability that random winners would pass; null when not computed.

lonePeaks.description: Folds won by a lone peak.

pooled.description: Pooled out-of-sample figures, each a state.

unreadable.description: Why the stored record could not be read; then no figure is given. Null for a readable record.

minTrades.description: The minimum sample the figures were judged against: the larger of the report minimum and the record's own.

ExitSelectionView.description: A stored exit choice for one cell. `Stable` is null when the record makes no statement, and `StabilityReason` says why.

ExperimentJobFinished.description: Client event `experimentFinished`: the last event of a job, with its final state.

ExperimentJobProgress.description: Client event `experimentProgress` (spec P8-18 Part B): a job entered a stage or advanced in it; at most four a second.

ExperimentJobView.description: A replay job as the screen shows it (spec P8-18 Part B).

name.description: The knob name from the preview, for example `FIXED_RR.rr` or `slippage.ticks`.

ExperimentKnobRequest.description: The knob of a replay: exactly one thing changed.

ExperimentPreviewView.description: What starting a replay on a baseline would mean, before the owner clicks (spec P8-18 criterion 12). Read only. Every look is a trial: the number it would be, the improvement it would have to show, the folds the data has and the best it can be called.

targetStatus.description: `met` or `not_met` only at exactly 214 instruments, else `not_comparable`.

ExperimentTimingView.description: The replay time of a finished job, as it is printed (spec P8-18 criterion 10): measured on this machine, with the instrument count and whether other heavy jobs ran.

experimentKey.description: The hash that identifies the experiment.

holdOutStart.description: First day of the hold-out that was not read, or null when none was kept.

trials.description: The experiments of the last 30 days when it was judged, itself included.

requiredImprovementR.description: The improvement required, mean R per trade.

pooledBaselineMeanR.description: Pooled mean R of the baseline over the used folds, or null.

baselineTotalR.description: Total R of the baseline after the live gap.

expectedLiveGapR.description: The live gap assumed, R per trade.

compareMs.description: Milliseconds spent reading both runs and judging them (measured); the replay is not included and not measured.

reasons.description: Why it is not better; empty when better.

reportText.description: The report with its honest limits; empty in a list.

parameters.description: The rules used; empty in a list.

ExperimentView.description: An experiment as the API shows it (P6-11, ADR 0072). The report text and the parameters are empty in a list and filled for one experiment.

format.description: csv (the default and the only format).

oneOf.description: The query of the screen the table is on, with the same field names as the GET of that screen; the page fields (limit, cursor) are ignored. There is deliberately no field for the charge-sheet confirmation.

ExportRequest.description: The body of an export (spec P8-20). There is no password, no actor and no file name in it: the actor is the session, the name is made by the server.

ExpressionRunList.description: The newest stored expression runs, newest first; State is `unavailable` with the reason `no_runs` when none is stored.

ExpressionRunSummary.description:
A stored expression run (spec P14-16): the profile, the counts paired and unpaired by reason, and the shares of the paired trades that used the model price, a derived expiry or the recent-archive spread, and per lot-feasibility word. The counts are of the whole run,
hold-out included; no figure of return, price or IV is shown.

ExtensionEvaluationList.description: The newest evaluations of a family, newest first, at most 100.

ExtensionEvaluationView.description:
One stored evaluation as the API shows it (P15-10): the verdict with the named missing quantities, the counts, the stated limits and the three JSON blocks as JSON (estimates with their intervals, the evidence block, the inputs). A value that is unavailable is the text
`unavailable` inside those blocks, never a number.

ExtractionCoverageRow.description: Counts of stored extractions for the coverage view (no text): by month of the announcement, model, prompt, schema and state.

ExtractionCoverageView.description: The coverage of the LLM announcement flag (P15-08): counts per month of the announcement, model file hash, prompt version, schema version and state. No text, no reason, no answer; the model hash is a file hash, not a path.

FacetCount.description: A filter value and how many active instruments have it.

feature.description: The feature name, or `f<index>` when the catalog of the model is not the current one.

meanAbsContribution.description: For a model the mean absolute contribution over its training rows; for one score the signed contribution.

FeatureImportanceView.description: The weight of one feature in a model or in one score: a path-based contribution in raw-score units (not exact, not SHAP).

FetchNowInput.description: Fetch now: the given baskets (the sources are turned on by this owner act) or, without ids, every enabled source; `force` overrides only the tripwire. An owner act: needs a step-up.

FetchOutcomeView.description: One fetch: `outcome` unchanged · applied · rejected · failed · skipped; `error` is the short reason of a rejection (tripwire, too_many_changes, row_count, bad_header, unmatched, not_csv, http_404 ...) or failure. No file content.

FilingCoverageView.description: The coverage of the filing store between `From` and `To`: counts only.

FilingFactView.description: One stored fact of a filing: a field for a span and basis, its state (`value` or `unavailable`), the number as filed or the reason, and the unit.

FilingFactsView.description: `GET /api/filings/{id}/facts`: the parse outcome of one filing with the parser version, the stored facts and the counts the parser kept (skipped contexts, sanity flags). `Outcome` is `not_parsed` until the parse step has run. No file content, no path.

FilingKindCoverage.description: One kind: `State` is `value` when anything is stored in the range, else `unavailable` (never a bare zero); `InstrumentsWithout` counts tracked instruments with no filing of the kind in the range.

FilingListView.description: Envelope metadata, at most 200 rows. With `asOf` the `State` is the point-in-time state (`value`, `none_visible`, `unavailable`) and `UnavailableCount` the filings of the instrument and kind without a broadcast time; without it both are null/0.

FilingQuarterCoverage.description: Counts of one kind in one quarter (by the period end, else the broadcast or ingest date in India time): `Ok` with a time, `Unavailable` without one, `Superseded` by a later revision, `OutOfOrder` stored unlinked.

FilingReasonCount.description: A count of stored filings without a broadcast time, by closed reason (`absent`, `date_only`, `no_offset`, `unparsable`, `before_2000`, `broadcast_in_future`).

FilingView.description: Metadata of one envelope (no file content, no path, no source reference).

status.description: `graded` (R measured against the plan's level) or `uncertain` (a pre-existing position or an oversized exit: no R), or `no_plan_levels` (the round trip is real but the plan grade has no entry or stop to measure it against; R is then empty).

entryPrice.description: Volume-weighted entry price of the fills.

exitPrice.description: Volume-weighted exit price of the fills.

planEntryPrice.description: The plan grade's simulated entry; null when none.

planStopPrice.description: The plan grade's simulated initial stop; null when none.

planR.description: The plan grade's R beside it; null when the ticket was not graded as a trade.

slippagePrice.description: Entry price paid minus the plan entry, signed so that positive is worse for the owner; null without a plan entry.

slippageR.description: The same in R (divided by the planned risk per share); null without plan levels.

charges.description: The charges the sync recorded for the fills used, rupees.

r.description: Realised result in R after the recorded charges; null without plan levels.

isChargesDoubt.description: True when the grade is uncertain only because charges were not recorded (it says nothing about whether the position was the ticket's own).

FillGrade.description: The grade of what the owner's fills did on a ticket (P7-14, ADR 0093), stored beside the plan-price grade. A realised result, never a simulation: the label is always string FillGrade.Basis.

FirstImportInput.description:
Optional per-holding dates for the first import that happens when the portfolio settings are saved (ADR 0013). Without rows, every holding Dhan lists is
imported dated with the first import date (flagged default-date); a row (key from `holdings/preview`, acquisition date) overrides the date of its holding.
At most 5000 rows. Used only when the account is connected to Dhan and has no holdings yet.

FirstImportView.description:
What a first import did. Status: "imported" (the holdings were created; the counts say how many), "skipped" (the account already has holdings, nothing was
imported), "deferred" (the account is not connected to Dhan, or the Portfolio role is off: the first sync imports every holding, dated FirstImportDate) or
"failed" (the settings were saved but the import was not: ErrorCode is `portfolio.import_failed`, Cause the code of the reason, for example
`portfolio.not_connected`, `portfolio.sync_running`; Message says what to do; save again or press Sync now to retry). Imported counts holdings created, DefaultDated those
among them dated by the first import date, AlreadyImported keys the account had already, Unknown keys Dhan no longer lists. Redated counts the lots that
followed a changed first import date (imported lots still on the default date; they stay flagged as such), RedateSkipped the ones that could not follow
because they were closed before the new date; both are 0 when the date did not change or the account has no holdings (ADR 0015).

FreshnessCheck.description: Freshness against the trading calendar: the last bar and the last closed session; `daysBehind` counts trading days.

FullPeriodView.description: A full-period (in-sample) figure of one candidate in one cell. It is exploration and never reaches the verdict.

GapRow.description:
A session of an instrument with missing 1-minute bars (ADR 0017 §3). `date` is the India date, `expected` the bars a complete session has (from the trading
calendar), `found` what is stored, `attempts` how often a refetch was made. `status`: open · filled · unfillable (a refetch added nothing).
`lastAttemptAt` is the latest refetch (null before the first), `detectedAt` when the gap was found.

GapsOverview.description:
How many instrument-sessions are in each state (the Dhan phase's gap table): `open` (missing bars a refetch may still add), `unfillable` (a refetch added
nothing), `filled`; `lastDetectedAt` is when a gap was last found (null while there never was one).

GapsView.description: The outcomes of the checked chain sessions, or `unavailable` when no session was ever checked.

GateView.description: One gate of a verdict as served (spec P5-03, P5-04); `Actual` is null when it is not finite.

points.description: One per plan-day, by date then plan.

GradeCurve.description: The top-K curve by rank: its points day by day and its totals.

curves.description: Top-1, top-3, top-5 and top-all by rank over primary and reserve tickets.

decisions.description: Approved, modified, rejected, lapsed and undecided (primary and reserve tickets only).

comparisons.description: Did the reserve, the rejection and the owner's refusals help.

GradeReportData.description: The numbers of doc 10 section 8 over a set of graded tickets (P7-13, ADR 0090).

meanR.description: Mean R per triggered ticket; null with none.

winRate.description: Share of triggered tickets with R above zero; null with none.

note.description: The honest note on the sample size; null when the sample reaches int GradeReport.IndicativeBelow.

GradeStats.description: The figures of a set of graded tickets (P7-13). R is summed over the graded (triggered) tickets only; the others add nothing and are counted.

meanDifference.description: Mean R of the first minus mean R of the second; null when either has no triggered ticket.

verdict.description: first_better, second_better, equal or not_enough_data. Never a claim of significance.

note.description: The sample-size note.

GroupComparison.description: Two sets compared by mean R per triggered ticket (P7-13): what the second would have added or avoided.

firstDate.description: Earliest entry date; null without a trade.

lastDate.description: Latest exit date; null without a trade.

provisional.description: A contributing run is marked provisional.

runKeys.description: The runs behind the trades, sorted.

GroupEvidenceView.description: What stands behind the figures of one group: its trades, the dates they span, whether any contributing run is provisional and which runs they came from.

GroupPart.description: The value of the holdings of a group that fall in one part of the second dimension (an account for sectors, a sector for accounts); the parts sum to the group's value.

value.description: The value; null when the run or trade did not record it.

GroupPartView.description: One coordinate of a group: the dimension (lower case) and its value; a null value is "not recorded".

key.description: The coordinates as text, `strategy=ORB|side=BUY`; `all` for the whole population.

profitFactor.description: Winning R over absolute losing R.

maxDrawdownR.description: Largest peak-to-trough fall of the running R.

longestLossStreak.description: Most losing trades in a row.

shrunkWinRate.description: The win rate shrunk toward its parent group.

winRateLower.description: Lower end of the credible interval of the shrunk win rate.

shrunkExpectancyR.description: Expectancy from the shrunk win rate and payoffs.

expectancyLowerR.description: Expectancy from the lower credible win rate and the shrunk payoffs: the ranking figure.

GroupView.description: One group of a report on the wire: who it is, its trade count and every figure as a MetricView (a number only for value or provisional), with the evidence of the group.

dimensions.description: The dimensions grouped by, in order.

nonAdditive.description: A trade appears in more than one group.

GroupsView.description: The groups of a report for a lens, in a fixed order (a value that was not recorded last), with the evidence of the report. bool GroupsView.NonAdditive is true when the basket dimension put a trade into more than one group, so the groups must not be summed.

recent.description: Losses with the tag in the latest window.

earlier.description: Losses with the tag in the window before.

GrowingTagView.description: A tag whose share rose between two windows of losses.

HalfLifeView.description: The half-lives (in sessions) of the pairs a formation selected: how many, the smallest, the median and the largest; `unavailable` when it selected none.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS act. It is checked on every request after the switch (an earlier step-up window does not count and is not used up); wrong ones count toward the sign-in lockout.

HistoryActRequest.description: The body of a history owner act (CF-04e). The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session.

HistoryBackfillStarted.description: The answer: bool HistoryBackfillStarted.Started false when nothing is pending (no run); else the service run that carries the work.

HistoryBenchmark.description:
The benchmark of a history. `State` is `ok` (the benchmark lines are filled) or `unavailable` with the `Reason` in words. `Symbol` is the canonical symbol and `Name` the display name of the index (null when the master list has
no such index). `Tracked`: tracking is on; `HasBars`: 1-minute bars are stored (the day bars follow when the aggregates are built). A screen offers "Track the benchmark" when it is unavailable and not tracked.
`AsOf` is the date of the last index close the benchmark lines were valued at (null when unavailable): the index has no live quote, so the benchmark lines end there and a live point of today (portfolio at today's prices) has no benchmark value.

HistoryCoverage.description:
How much of the open holdings the history covers: `Holdings` open holdings, `Covered` of them have stored day bars, `Unpriced` have none (not tracked, not in the instrument master, or bars not fetched yet:
they are left out and never valued at zero). `LateStart` counts covered holdings whose bars begin after their earliest lot, so part of their history is missing.

HistoryPoint.description:
One day of the portfolio history (rupees; `Nav` and `BenchmarkNav` start at 100). `Value` is what the lots held that day were worth at the day's close (adjusted prices), `Invested` what
they cost. `BenchmarkValue` is the same cash flows put into the benchmark index; it and `BenchmarkNav` are null when the benchmark has no history for the series.

HistorySwitchView.description: The switch, read-only: the owner cannot turn it on from the web (CF-04e decision D1).

HoldOutPlanView.description: The sizing the policy gives for the stored history now (D4).

HoldOutResultView.description:
What the one look at the hold-out said, as served and as stored (spec CF-06, D5). `State` is `used` (the first look at the block) or `reused` (a later look: the numbers are shown, the result counts as a trial and cannot count toward a pass).
`Mode` is `owner` or `auto` (the auto option, recorded as auto and never as an owner approval). `RunSawHoldOut` is true when the run the plan came from had a window reaching into the block: such a look is never a pass.

HoldOutUnlockRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/lab/runs/{id}/holdout-unlock` (spec CF-06, D5): the owner's password, typed again for this act.

HoldOutView.description: `GET /api/lab/holdout`: the block (or what it would be), whether the Lab enforces it, and every look taken. Numbers appear only in an unlock that was taken.

HoldingGroup.description:
One group. Key is the account id, bucket id, sector name or basket id, or `~none` for the sector "Unclassified" and the basket "No basket". Holdings counts every holding of the group in the scope;
Unpriced the open ones without a usable price. DayChangeExcluded counts the open holdings left out of the day change. Parts is set only when the request had a `stackBy`. Income is the group's dividends and trade
charges and the net returns (ADR 0026), null when none is recorded; a group by account also holds the account's own dividends and costs (those of no holding). The group with the key `~unallocated` (name "Unallocated", no holdings,
no value) is added last when dividends and costs belong to no group, so that the columns add up to the total.

HoldingGroupTotal.description: The scope's totals, computed once over every holding of the scope (for basket groupings this is not the sum of the groups). WeightPct is 100 when the scope has a value. Income includes the dividends and costs of no holding.

HoldingGroups.description:
The groups of the scope. By is `account`, `bucket`, `sector` or `basket`; Additive is false for baskets (a holding is in every basket that contains it, so the groups overlap). StackBy is the second dimension of the
parts, when asked for. At most 200 groups are returned.

HoldingLots.description: The lots of a holding, open lots first (oldest first), then closed ones.

HoldingPage.description: One page of holdings (Total counts all matches).

HoldingRebuildResult.description: The rebuild of one holding's lots: with `DryRun` only what it would do; otherwise `Applied` says whether the lots were replaced (only an `ok` rebuild is).

HoldingRow.description:
One holding. Status is "open" or "closed". Mapped is false when the holding is not in the instrument master (InstrumentId and CanonicalSymbol are
then null). LotCount counts open lots; EarliestAcquiredOn is the oldest open lot's date; UsesDefaultDate is true when any open lot has the
import's default date. Returns cover all lots (closed lots add to RealisedPnl and to the XIRR).
PreviousClose is the previous session's close as the last quote reported it (null until a quote gave one). DayChange (rupees) and DayChangePct (percent number) are
against it, for an open, priced holding with a previous close; otherwise both are null and the holding is left out of the summary's day change. PriceAt is the time of
LastPrice (the same instant as LastPriceAt) and PriceSource says where the price came from: "sync" (the holdings list at the last sync), "quote" (a market quote) or "live" (a tick of the live feed).
Income is the holding's dividends and trade charges and the net returns that include them (ADR 0026); null when nothing is recorded for the holding. It does not change with the price, except the two total return percentages: the
browser works those out again at a live price from Returns.RealisedPnl, Returns.Pnl, Returns.Invested and Income's Dividends and Charges.

HoldingsSummary.description:
Totals over the holdings of the filter (all accounts that count in totals, one account, one bucket). DefaultDateLots counts open lots that
still have the import's default date. UnpricedCount counts open holdings without a usable price: they are left out of Returns (invested, value, P&L, XIRR). ValuationDate is the day the values are as of (today in India).
DayChange (rupees) is the sum of the day changes of the included open holdings and DayChangePct (percent number) is that sum over the sum of qty x previous close of the same holdings; both are null when no
holding is included. DayChangeExcluded counts the open holdings left out (no previous close or no usable price). PricesAsOf holds the oldest and the newest price time of the open priced holdings.
BenchmarkXirr (percent number) is the XIRR of the same cash flows put into the benchmark index (Nifty 50 by default, ADR 0020 §2), Alpha the portfolio's XIRR minus it in percentage points; BenchmarkState is "ok", "unavailable" (the index has no history
from the first cash flow: track it and run Update data), "insufficient" (the same reasons as for XIRR) or "n_m" (beyond ±1,000 %). BenchmarkXirr and Alpha are null unless their rates are meaningful (Alpha also needs the portfolio's XirrState "ok").
BenchmarkAsOf is the date of the index close the benchmark was valued at: the index has no live quote, so on a trading day before its bar is fetched it is the previous close while the portfolio is valued at today's prices. AlphaBasis says which
it is when Alpha is set: "last_close" (portfolio and index are both as of their last close) or "live_vs_last_close" (the portfolio at prices of a later trading day than the index close, so the alpha includes the day's move of the portfolio only).
Alpha compares price returns: the gross XIRR and the index's price index, both before dividends and charges (ADR 0026). Income holds the dividends and costs of the scope and the net returns (null when nothing is recorded): for the whole portfolio or
an account (no bucket) it includes the dividends not allocated to a holding and the ledger's costs, for a bucket only its holdings'.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code, e.g. auth.invalid_credentials, auth.locked, auth.session_expired, auth.csrf_invalid, auth.step_up_required, accounts.not_found, accounts.invalid (field errors in "errors"), accounts.conflict, accounts.app_not_configured, accounts.broker_error (502), accounts.connect_mismatch, accounts.consent_limit (429), accounts.connect_expired, accounts.connect_cancelled, portfolio.not_connected, portfolio.sync_running, portfolio.confirmation_required and portfolio.confirmation_stale (409, with listedHoldings, openHoldings and wouldClose), portfolio.conflict (409), portfolio.invalid, portfolio.not_found, portfolio.lot_from_trade (409), portfolio.preview_stale (409, with report), services.not_found (404), services.invalid (400, with issues), services.revision_changed (409), services.already_running (409), services.read_only (409), history.disabled, history.disk_low, history.calendar_missing, history.outside_window (422), history.run_active (409), history.no_target (404).

retryAfterSeconds.description: Present on auth.locked, auth.rate_limited and accounts.consent_limit: seconds until a new attempt may succeed.

openHoldings.description: Present on portfolio.confirmation_required and portfolio.confirmation_stale: how many holdings the account has open.

listedHoldings.description: Present on portfolio.confirmation_required and portfolio.confirmation_stale: how many holdings Dhan listed.

issues.description: Present on services.invalid: every error of the refused schedule - the service it is about (serviceId; absent for the service of the request), the field (a dotted path like the request, e.g. schedule.time, retries, parameters.x), severity (error), a stable code and the text.

report.description: Present on portfolio.preview_stale: the fresh preview of the file, in the shape of the response of POST /api/portfolio/trades/preview (TradePreviewReport).

wouldClose.description: Present on portfolio.confirmation_required: how many of them the sync would close because Dhan no longer lists them.

text.description: A plain sentence, including what was not done.

HypothesisStepView.description: One row of a hypothesis's history.

state.description: proposed, approved, running, judged, accepted, rejected or expired.

cellKey.description: The cell it is about, or null.

baselineValue.description: The value in the baseline run.

experimentId.description: The experiment that judged it, once judged.

reason.description: The reason of the newest move.

nextStates.description: The states it may move to.

history.description: Every step, oldest first; empty in a list.

note.description: What an accepted hypothesis does and does not do.

HypothesisView.description: A hypothesis as the API shows it (P6-10, ADR 0076): the newest row of its log, with the legal next states and, for one hypothesis, its history.

ImportCorporateActionsResult.description:
The outcome of a CSV import (or its preview). `lines`: data lines read; `importable`: new valid actions; `imported`: written (0 for a preview); `duplicates`: lines that repeat an action
that exists (any status) or an earlier line; `invalid`: lines with a problem (the first 50 in `errors`, among them lines that clash with an applied action of the other kind on the same day);
`unknownSymbols`: symbols that match no listed instrument (never guessed). `adjustsCsvTwice`: how many of the importable lines have an ex-date on or before the date their instrument's loaded
CSV files reach, listed in `warnings` (the first 50); an import (not a preview) with such lines needs `acknowledgeCsvAdjusted=true`, else 409 `data.csv_already_adjusted`.

ImportFileError.description: Why a file could not be read or imported: `portfolio.invalid` (`Field``file`), `portfolio.wrong_file_kind` (an unknown shape; the message lists the accepted kinds), `portfolio.preview_stale`, `portfolio.other_account`, `portfolio.sync_running`, `portfolio.conflict`.

ImportFilePreview.description:
What a file is and what importing it would do — nothing is stored. `Kind`: `global_transaction_report`, `dp_charges`, `demat_holding`, `pnl_report`, `trades` (a tradebook with a buy/sell column), `dividends`, `tradebook_without_sides`,
`statement`, `unknown`. `Supported` is true when the file can be imported here. A file that belongs on another screen has `RouteTo` (`dividends`); one that cannot be imported has a `Message` saying why; a file that cannot be read has an `Error`. Of
the blocks only the one of the kind is set: `Trades` (the tradebook preview: global transaction report and tradebook) with `Bill` beside it for the global transaction report, `Costs` (depository charges), `Demat`. `Digest` fingerprints what is shown;
an import sends it back.

ImportFileResult.description:
What importing one file did. `Status`: `imported` (something was stored), `nothing_new` (nothing to store: the file is imported already), `not_supported` (the kind cannot be imported; `Message` says why), `rejected` (`Error` says why; a
`portfolio.preview_stale` error comes with the fresh `Preview` and nothing was stored). Of the results only the one of the kind is set: `Trades` (global transaction report and tradebook), `Costs`, `Demat`. `AliasesSaved` counts the choices remembered.

ImportLineError.description: A line of an imported text that could not be used, with the reason (no free text from the file is repeated).

ImportLineWarning.description:
A valid line whose ex-date is on or before the date the instrument's loaded CSV files reach (`csvAdjustedThrough`): importing it would adjust those already adjusted prices twice.
`symbol` is the canonical symbol (`NSE:ABB`).

ImportPreview.description: What Dhan holds for the account, nothing saved. DefaultDate is the account's first import date (2025-01-01 until the owner chooses another).

ImportPreviewResponse.description: The previews of the files of one request, in the order they were sent.

ImportRowInput.description: One holding to import (a key from the preview). AcquiredOn left out means "use the first import date" (the lot is then flagged).

ImportRunResponse.description: The results of the files of one request, in the order they were sent.

ImportSummary.description: The counts every kind of file has. `Rows` are the data rows, `Valid` the rows that can be used, `ToAdd` what an import would store, `AlreadyImported` what is stored already, `Skipped` the valid rows left out (by reason in the kind's own block), `Bad` the rows that cannot be used. `From`/`To` are the period the report says it covers.

ImportWarning.description: A notice about a file. `Code`: `other_account` (the report's client code differs from that of the reports imported into the account before; the account remembers a hash of the first code, never the code), `charges_differ_from_footer`, `needs_match` (`Count` names that could not be tied to a security), `partial_name_match`, `negative_charges`, `value_not_reproduced`, `covered_by_dhan`, `totals_differ`, `bad_rows`, `holdings_differ` (a demat statement and the synced holdings differ; nothing is changed), `notice_only` (the file is recognised and not imported).

IncomeView.description:
What a scope (a holding, a group, an account, the portfolio) received and paid beyond its price return (ADR 0026, P2-14). Money is rupees, percentages are percent numbers (16.1 = 16.1 %), dates are India dates. `Dividends` are the
dividends the owner entered (not voided) and `Charges` the trade charges of the stored trades plus, for an account and the portfolio only, the ledger's costs of the account as such (DP charges, annual maintenance, delayed-payment interest ...;
never the costs of trades, which the trade rows already carry). `LedgerCharges` is that ledger part of `Charges` (0 when the account has none; null when the scope does not include account-level items: a holding, a bucket), so the screen can show
the ledger's costs apart from the charges of trades. `Unallocated` is the part of the dividends not allocated to a holding (set for an account and the portfolio only, otherwise null). `TotalReturnPct` is (realised + unrealised +
dividends) over invested, `NetTotalReturnPct` the same minus the charges; both are null when nothing is invested or the scope has no usable price. `NetXirr` is the XIRR of the lot cash flows plus the dividends (in) and the charges (out) on
their dates, with `NetXirrState` as for the gross XIRR (`ok`, `insufficient`, `n_m`, `no_data`, `no_price`).
Only what was entered or read is counted, and the dates say from when each source is known (null: the source has nothing for the scope): `DividendsFrom` is the first dividend the owner entered, `TradeChargesFrom` the first stored trade that
carries charges (trades read before charges were stored, and CSV or manual trades, carry none — so a trade without charges is "unknown", not "free"), `LedgerChargesFrom` the first ledger date stored. `ChargesFrom` is the later of
`TradeChargesFrom` and `LedgerChargesFrom` when both exist, otherwise the one that does. `CoverageFrom` is the LATER start of the sources that exist for the scope: the date from which every kind of income that is counted at all is known, so
the net figures are never presented as complete from before any of their sources begins. The whole object is null when the scope has no dividend and no charge recorded.

IndexBenchmarkView.description: The price return of the benchmark index over the same window.

IndexDifferenceView.description: The basket's hold return, the index's over the same dates and their difference, all in percent and all passive.

kind.description: The rule: best_strategy, weakest_strategy, basket_gap, side_bias, best_exit, weekday, regime or calibration.

cells.description: The keys of the cells the figures were read from.

InsightView.description: One auto-insight (doc 15 section 6): a fixed-template sentence. string InsightView.State is `value` when the sentence states something; otherwise the text says why it states nothing and carries no figure.

InsightsView.description: The eight auto-insights, always in the same order, with the evidence of the report.

InstrumentBars.description:
The latest bars of an instrument and timeframe, newest first. `adjustment` is set only when the read asked for adjusted prices (`adjusted=true`): the bars then have the open, high, low and close multiplied by
the cumulative factor of the corporate actions applied after their date, rounded to 4 decimals, and the volume divided by it; the block says which actions and what factor (see AdjustmentView).

InstrumentBasketView.description: A basket that holds an instrument now; `since` = when it was added.

InstrumentDetail.description: Everything the master list knows about an instrument.

InstrumentPage.description: One page of search results (`total` counts all matches).

InstrumentPrice.description:
The latest known price of an instrument: `lastPrice` at `priceAt` (the time of the exchange's tick for `live`, the time of the quote for `quote`, the time of the sync for `sync`; UTC) and where it came from:
`live` (the live feed), `quote` (the 5-minute quote poll) or `sync` (the broker's holdings list). The same values as `lastPrice`, `priceAt` and `priceSource` of the holdings list. An older price never follows a newer one
for the same instrument; a client that gets one anyway ignores it.

InstrumentSummary.description: A row of the master list. `type`: share · etf · index · future.

InstrumentsWithoutEntryView.description: The tracked instruments that have no visible upcoming results meeting at the question (the count and the first 300 symbols). Their `days_to_results` is unavailable, never a default.

IpAttestationRequest.description: The owner's attestation of the static IP. The actor is never taken from the body.

status.description: open (not finished), pending (finished, plan grade not there yet), graded, no_plan_levels or uncertain (no R).

oneOf.description: The fill grade, labelled `realised fills, not simulated`; null until graded.

planStatus.description: The plan-price grade's status, or pending.

planR.description: The plan-price grade's R, labelled `simulated on plan prices`.

uncertain.description: Why the round trip may not be the ticket's alone (shares held before it); no R is written then.

JournalEntryView.description: One ticket's journal line: plan grade and fill grade side by side.

JournalFillView.description: A fill as the API shows it.

basis.description: gross, costed_unconfirmed or net_confirmed; null with no counterfactual.

population.description: The run keys behind the counterfactual.

to.description: The last day of the data.

JourneyEvidenceView.description: What the numbers on the Journey rest on.

JourneyLiveView.description: The live line, which is never evaluable until real trades exist.

state.description: ok, or empty when no ticket is graded.

note.description: Truncation or other caveat, or null.

JourneyPlanPriceView.description: The plan-price line: grades by week.

oneOf.description: The newest stored counterfactual's header, or null.

evidence.description: Basis, population, range, n and limits.

meanR.description: Mean R; null when the week is insufficient.

JourneyWeekView.description: One ISO week of graded plan tickets.

proposalOnly.description: True for the CF-09 failure boundary: the automatic setting never executes it, only the owner applies it.

trades.description: Trades the figure is based on.

cells.description: The cells it would pause (Paper or Active when proposed).

settingsHash.description: The SHA-256 of the settings that produced it.

proposedOn.description: The India date it was proposed.

decidedAt.description: When it was decided, or null.

autoSettingId.description: For an automatic decision, the switch row in force; else null.

dismissReason.description: The owner's reason when the proposal was dismissed, else null.

KillProposalView.description: One kill proposal as the owner reads it.

settings.description: The automatic setting and the thresholds.

KillProposalsView.description: The proposals and the settings beside them.

auto.description: Whether an automatic demotion is allowed now (default OFF).

settingId.description: The row of the switch in force, or null when none was ever stored.

KillSettingsView.description: The automatic setting and the thresholds as they stand.

auto.description: The new value of `confidence.kill.auto` (default OFF): ON lets the daily decay-monitor demote the cells of a strategy when a kill rule fires, except for the CF-09 failure boundary.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS change, ON or OFF. It is checked on every request (a step-up window opened earlier does not count); wrong ones count toward the sign-in lockout. Missing: 403 auth.step_up_required.

KillSwitchRequest.description: The body of the automatic kill switch. The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session.

KillSwitched.description: The answer of a switch change: the row and the new value.

LabCounts.description: The counts of a finished run: the instruments asked for and replayed, the ones skipped, and the trades (closed and open at the end of the data).

LabInstrument.description: One instrument of a Lab run's universe.

LabProblem.description: One located problem of a run, with the stage that found it.

LabProgressView.description: Where a running run is: instruments done of instruments in total (0 and 0 outside the quick test).

LabReportView.description:
The report of a finished full or robust test (spec P5-06, doc 11 §4), built from the stored result only. `NotIncluded` names the sections of doc 11 §4 that the stored result cannot fill, so nothing is invented. `DeflatedSharpe` (CF-03) is the probability beside the factor, null when not computed. `CostStress` (CF-05) is the cost stress and the delay test, null when not computed. `Trials`, `Registration` and `HoldOut` (CF-06) are the count of looks with its parts, the pre-registration state and the hold-out state; null in a report built without them. `Nulls` (CF-07) is the random-entry null, null when not computed. `Summary` is a deterministic
template over the numbers above, not an assistant text.

LabRunFinished.description: Client event `labRunFinished` (spec P5-02, D5): the last event of a run, with its final state.

LabRunOptionsView.description: The options a run was posted with, as the effective values (CF-05, ADR 0229): `slippage` is `default` or `conservative`; `stress` is whether the cost stress block was wanted (on for `robust` unless posted off, off for the others unless posted on). `Nulls` is false when the chance and plateau block was posted left out (CF-07, ADR 0231) and `Draws` is the posted number of random-entry seeds (null: the configured number). `IsDefault` is true when all are what a post without options gets; only such a run may be the scorecard's evidence basis.

LabRunProgress.description: Client event `labRunProgress` (spec P5-02, D5): a run entered a stage or advanced in it. `done` and `total` count instruments in the quick test and are 0 elsewhere.

LabRunView.description:
A Lab run as the API serves it (spec P5-02, Contract): the same data the hub's events carry, so a missed event costs nothing. `verdict` is always null in this slice (P5-03); `labels` carry the cost basis, the sample and the line that a
quick test is exploration, not a verdict (D6).

LabStageLog.description: One entry of the stage log: when a stage began and ended and how many problems it found.

LabStrategyRef.description: The strategy version a run tests.

isDated.description: True for a basket run that replays each day with that day's members (BK-11b): its requests name the basket and the basis, not the list.

LabUniverse.description:
The universe of a Lab run as it was resolved when the run was posted (spec P5-02, D2): the basket changes later, the run keeps the list. Requested is the number of members before the quick-test sample;
Sampled says the list was cut to the limit by the seeded shuffle of Seed.

LabVerdictView.description: The verdict of a full test with everything it rests on (spec P5-04): outcome, gates, limits, the cells and the exploration block. `DeflatedSharpe` (CF-03) is the probability beside the heuristic factor; null in a result stored before it or when its mode is Off. `CostStress` (CF-05) is the cost stress and the delay test beside the outcome; null in a result stored before it or when its mode is Off. `Trials` (CF-06) is the count of looks with its parts as of the judgement; null in a result stored before it. `Nulls` (CF-07) is the random-entry null beside the outcome; null in a result stored before it, in a run that is not robust or when its mode is Off. `Benchmark` (CF-11 row 13, ADR 0227) is the daily Sharpe of the strategy against its universe's buy-and-hold; null in a result stored before it.

LabWindow.description: The India dates a run replays, inclusive.

LastDataJobs.description: The latest job in which each phase ran to an end (null when none did yet).

hash.description: The first 12 characters of its hash.

sessionDate.description: The newest session of the run.

LearnedAllowedSetting.description: An allow-listed key with its label, its safer direction and the bounds.

LearnedChangeView.description:
One change. `Direction` is tighten or loosen. `State` is proposed, applied, dismissed or undone. `DecidedBy` is `auto` (never shown as an owner approval) or `owner:<e-mail>`. `ApproveNeedsPassword` is true for a loosening;
`CanUndo` is true for an applied change and `UndoNeedsPassword` says whether the undo loosens (undoing a tightening always does).

LearnedChangesView.description: `AutoOn`: the Auto switch (OFF by default). `WeeklyCap` and `AutoAppliedThisWeek`: the guardrail and what it has used in the trailing 7 days. `TakesEffect`: when an applied change is read by the host. `Allowlist`: the keys learning may touch.

LearnedPasswordRequest.description: The body of an approve or an undo: the owner's password, re-entered for THIS act. Needed when the act loosens a gate (a loosening proposal, and any undo of a tightening); ignored otherwise. The owner is never part of the body.

cellRows.description: Rows in the newest cell-statistics snapshot (all windows).

cellsAsOf.description: The as-of date of that snapshot, or null before the first computation.

LearningOverviewView.description: What the Learning screen needs first (P6-18, ADR 0080): counts and the newest verdicts of the stored learning records. Read from the stores; no statistic is computed and no model is scored.

elapsedMs.description: Milliseconds this read took (the check re-reads two runs).

LearningPhaseCheckView.description: The P6 exit criteria from stored records (P8-04).

verdict.description: MET, NOT MET or NOT EVALUABLE.

caveat.description: What a MET rests on without being verified here; null when none.

LedgerClassTotal.description: The entries of one class in the period and their signed total.

LedgerEntryView.description:
A ledger entry. `Class` is `funds_in`, `funds_out`, `dividend`, `charges` or `other`; `Amount` is signed (credit minus debit). `Description` and `Narration` are Dhan's free text (untrusted: show as plain text).
`Source` is `broker` (read from Dhan's ledger) or `import` (a cost imported from a downloaded report, such as the depository-charges sheet, which can be undone).

LedgerPage.description:
One page of the ledger, newest first, and the totals of every class for the period (`from` to `to`, whatever class is filtered). `CoverageFrom` is the earliest date of any ledger entry stored for the account, whatever the filters
(null: none stored): the ledger's costs are known from this date on, which reading from an earlier date can move back (ADR 0026).

LedgerRowView.description: One ledger row as the API shows it (`window` is the posted window).

LedgerView.description: The ledger of a family, the number of variants in it and the factor the gates are tightened by now (1 when the adjustment is off). `Trials` (CF-06) is the honest count of looks with its parts.

LessonStepView.description: One row of a lesson's history.

experimentId.description: The linked or resolved experiment, or null.

experimentOutcome.description: Outcome of the experiment the result was read from.

beforeMeanR.description: Pooled mean R before (baseline), or null.

afterMeanR.description: Pooled mean R after (candidate), or null.

reason.description: The reason of the newest move.
