An account on the ramp. `step` is null while no step is set (no live allocation). `scaleEffective` is the factor of the step; the live risk is the intended risk times it. `eligible` is true only when G1 to G6 all pass; an unreadable gate
is never a pass.

trades.description: How many of them were restated with random entries (the real mean is the mean of these).

validSeeds.description: Seeds with at least one random trade.

realMeanR.description: Mean net R of the restated real trades; null when no trade could be restated.

percentile.description: The configured percentile (95), which sets the level of the test.

percentileValue.description: The seed means at that percentile.

countAtLeast.description: Seeds whose mean is at least the real mean.

threshold.description: The level of the test, `1 - percentile / 100`.

comparison.description: How the value is read against the threshold (`<=`).

droppedShare.description: Share of the (trade, seed) draws dropped after the redraws.

seed.description: The seed of the run for this null, as text.

RandomEntryView.description:
The random-entry null of one Lab verdict (CF-07, D1): the real mean net R against the means of int RandomEntryView.Draws seeds, each a full set of random-entry trades with the real trades' instrument, session, side, risk fraction, target multiple and costs.
The reading is double? RandomEntryView.PValue against double RandomEntryView.Threshold: string RandomEntryView.Status is `pass` only when the p-value is at most the threshold; the percentiles are displayed, not a second test. `unavailable` is never a pass and
double? RandomEntryView.PValue is then null.

lowerBoundPositive.description: The lower bound of expectancy is above 0: the only reading of "works" the engine allows.

RankedCellView.description: A cell with enough sample in its place in the ranking by the credible lower bound of expectancy.

RankingRowView.description: One basket on the ranking board.

RateLine.description: A rate with its sample and its Wilson 95 % interval (spec P9-09 AC 9: every rate is printed with its interval).

warnings.description: What the owner must know: the CF-11 gates are not enforcing yet, and whether any kill condition was there to clear.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS act. Missing: 403 auth.step_up_required; wrong: 401, counted toward the lockout.

ReEnableRequest.description: The body of a re-enable. The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session.

share.description: Count over the trades with a recorded excursion.

ReachedMfeView.description: Trades whose favourable excursion reached the level, and their share of the trades with a recorded excursion.

labelOk.description: For gate S, whether the label is "Ready for the next phase"; true for gate R.

failing.description: The required rows that are not a pass.

ReadinessGateView.description: One gate with what stops it.

enforce.description: Whether a failed gate refuses a lifecycle move (ON) or only warns (OFF, the default; no row means OFF).

switchId.description: The row of the switch in force, or null when none was ever stored.

ReadinessSettingsView.description: The readiness settings now: the owner's switch and the thresholds beside it.

enforce.description: The new value of `confidence.readiness.enforce` (default OFF): ON makes a failed readiness gate refuse the lifecycle move it judges (Candidate to Paper, the re-enable of a paused cell, Paper to Active); OFF only warns.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS change, ON or OFF (turning it OFF removes a refusal). It is checked on every request; wrong ones count toward the sign-in lockout; missing: 403 auth.step_up_required.

ReadinessSwitchRequest.description: The body of the readiness enforce switch. The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session.

ReadinessSwitched.description: The answer of a switch change: the row and the new value.

ReasonCountView.description: A reserve reason and its count.

outcome.description: One of the outcomes of the kind (static_ip: not_needed_for_manual, requested, obtained, whitelisted, declined, blocked; sebi_recheck: rechecked_no_change, rechecked_changed, blocked; dhan_ip_read_policy: reads_not_ip_restricted, reads_ip_restricted, unanswered).

decidedOn.description: The India date of the decision; not in the future.

summary.description: 1 to 1000 characters of what you were told or read. No IP address, client id or token: they are refused.

sources.description: At most 10 sources, each an https:// URL or a circular id such as NSE/INVG/73992.

staticIpState.description: static_ip only: none, requested, active or whitelisted.

isp.description: static_ip only: the provider's name, up to 80 characters, no address.

whitelistedAt.description: static_ip only: the date set at Dhan; required when the state is whitelisted, refused otherwise.

nextReviewOn.description: After decidedOn and at most 400 days ahead.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS save. It is checked on every request (a step-up window opened earlier does not count and is not used up or extended); wrong ones count toward the sign-in lockout.

RecordComplianceRequest.description: The body of a compliance record (spec P11-05). The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session. The lock end is not part of it either: the server derives it.

RecoveryCounts.description: Headline counts, in rows (one row is one step of the ledger, which may cover several sessions, or one missed session of the plan; not sessions): missed (missed, waiting, running, not recoverable, out of reach), recovered, still failing (still failing, blocked, partial).

RecoveryPlanUnavailable.description: The plan of what a pass would do was refused (`Reason`): the rows of the ledger are shown, but "nothing missed" cannot be concluded.

RecoveryRetryAccepted.description: `Started` is true when the pass has steps to run (`Steps`); false when there is nothing to run, so the pass only proves partial items again.

RecoveryRowView.description: One service at one session. `From` to `To` are the sessions the step covers (the group is its last session); `MissingSessions` are those a partial recovery did not fill; `RetryKind` says what a retry does (null: nothing, `CanRetry` false), a failed step that used up its attempts is not run again.

RecoveryStatusView.description: `CheckedAt` is when this was read; `Running` is true while a pass runs; `Truncated` when the ledger held more rows than are shown (the newest sessions are kept). Sessions are oldest first.

RefreshRunView.description: One refresh run. `trigger`: manual · daily · forced; `status`: running · succeeded · unchanged · failed; `phase` (while running): downloading · parsing · enriching · saving.

RefreshStarted.description: The refresh that was registered; follow it with `GET /api/instruments/refresh/status`.

RefreshStatusView.description: Where the master list stands: the refresh in progress (if any), the last finished one, the automatic schedule and how many instruments are active.

RegimeBucketView.description: One regime part of the out-of-sample trades (P6-02): the regime and its basis are one bucket; below 30 trades it is shown but is not evidence.

RegimeCountView.description: How many sessions of the range fall in one regime, by basis; a regime with no session shows 0 (nothing is hidden).

RegimeDayView.description: The regime label of one session (P6-02): the regime read from the context day before it, or why there is none.

RegimeLabelsView.description:
The regime labels per session (`GET /api/data/regimes`, P6-02, ADR 0146): `Days` for the range asked, the counts per regime and basis and the sessions without a label by reason over the same range, and what the whole stored history makes readable
(`FirstLabel`, `FirstIndexAndVix`). The label of a session reads only data before it; the index is the regime index of the context (NIFTY 50 by default).

RegimeMissingView.description: Out-of-sample trades with no regime label, by reason (P6-02).

RegimeRowView.description: The index on days that followed one regime of the previous session.

RegimeUnavailableView.description: Sessions with no label, by reason.

RegistrationRequest.description: Body of `PUT /api/lab/strategies/{id}/versions/{v}/registration` (spec CF-06, D1): the five plain texts. The actor is the signed-in owner, never a field.

RegistrationView.description: The pre-registration of a strategy version as served (spec CF-06, D1): five plain texts (never markup), the hash of their canonical text, who wrote it and when. It is frozen once written.

RejectProposalRequest.description: The body of `POST /api/assistant/proposals/{id}/reject` (AC 10): an optional reason of at most 300 characters.

RelativeStrengthReturnView.description: The relative strength return over a window of sessions (fraction).

RelativeStrengthRowView.description: One stored row. `basketId` is the empty id for the index-relative row (lookback 20; `score` is percentage points).

RelativeStrengthView.description: The rows and the cap they were cut at.

ReleaseHaltRequest.description: The owner's release of a halt: a reason and the password, checked afresh for this act.

RemoveMembersInput.description: Instruments to remove from a basket (1 to 500; repeats count once).

RemoveMembersResult.description: What a removal did: `removed` were members, `notMembers` were not. Untracking never happens. `memberCount` = members now.

RepairBarHolesRequest.description: The body of the repair: the first and the last closed session of the window.

RepairBarHolesResult.description:
What the repair did. int RepairBarHolesResult.MissingAfter is what the broker could not give. int RepairBarHolesResult.Rejected counts bars the broker returned that failed the bar checks.
Guid? RepairBarHolesResult.AggregateJobId is the follow-up job, or null with string? RepairBarHolesResult.AggregateNote saying why not.

ReplayBarView.description: One bar: `t` is the epoch seconds of its start.

ReplayBlockedView.description: A candidate that was not taken, with its one reason.

ReplayBookTradeView.description: One trade of the replay book.

ReplayCancelView.description: The answer of a cancel: the new state, cancelled for a run that had not started and cancelling for one that is running.

adjusted.description: Always true: the bars are adjusted like the stored trade.

adjustedThrough.description: The ex-date of the last corporate action applied to the bars; null when none is.

coherence.description: Whether the bars agree with the stored entry.

ReplayChartView.description: The bars of the replay window at one timeframe, adjusted for the corporate actions applied now, with the coherence of the stored entry against them.

ReplayCoherenceView.description: `state` is ok, entry_mismatch or no_bars; `entryOnBars` is null with no bar.

ReplayCompleteness.description: How far a run has got (AC 14): bool ReplayCompleteness.Complete is true only for a run whose every session was replayed.

ReplayCostingView.description: What the run charged the trade. The figures are present only when the owner confirmed this very charge sheet (`confirmed`); otherwise only the sheet id is, and the screen says "costed on sheet X, not confirmed as yours" beside the gross figures.

ReplayEquityPoint.description: One day of the equity curve: the equity, the drawdown from the peak so far, the cash (equity less the cost of the positions open at the close) and the benchmark rebased to the capital.

ReplayEquityView.description: The equity curve of a run against its benchmark (Nifty 500 unless the owner chose another index for the basket reports).

ReplayFeatureItemView.description: One stored feature: its group (`bars`, `context`, `plan`), and a number only when `state` is value.

ReplayFeaturesView.description: The decision-time features stored for the trade (catalog `version`): `state` is value, or unavailable with the `reason` (no row stored, or a row of another decision). Never a zero for an unknown.

ReplayFigures.description: The figures of a run over the sessions stored so far; each is null where it cannot be told (too few sessions, no trades).

ReplayFillView.description: An entry replayed on the next session.

ReplayLabelView.description: One hindsight label: its code and the plain sentence the screen shows first (SR-01, AC 10).

ReplayLegView.description: One fill of a trade with legs: `kind` is entry, add or exit; `share` the fraction of the maximum quantity; `reason` empty for an entry or an add.

ReplayOpenPositionView.description: A position open at the close of the session.

ReplayPairView.description: The frozen-versus-learning comparison of a pair (AC 9), computed on read from the two stored runs. string? ReplayPairView.Answer is null while a run is not complete, with the reason.

ReplayRunListItem.description: One row of the list of runs.

ReplayRunView.description: The summary of one run: settings snapshot, hashes, hindsight labels first, completeness, figures and the costs label.

ReplayScopeBody.description: The baskets and instruments a replay covers; both empty means the owner's stored auto scope, its baskets' members read as of each session.

ReplaySessionListItem.description: One session of the list: what was taken, what was blocked by reason, the day's result and the equity.

ReplaySessionListView.description: The sessions of a run, one row each.

ReplaySessionView.description: The full record of one session.

ReplayStartBody.description: The body of the start of a replay (SR-01 part C). Defaults: to is the last readable session before the hold-out and its embargo, capital 1000000, the seeded standard profile, gross costs (costs null or "gross"; otherwise the id of a stored charge sheet), versions start (the version active today, a labelled hindsight), modes frozen.

ReplayStrategyContribution.description: What one strategy contributed: closed trades, result in rupees (net, or gross when the run is) and the sum of R.

ReplayTradeView.description: The stored facts of a replayed trade, in adjusted prices. Times are instants (the screen shows India time); a target is null without a fixed reward-to-risk, never zero.

window.description: The window and where it came from.

membersAsOf.description: The India date the members are as of; members as of that date, not as of each trading day (survivorship, ISS-22).

baskets.description: One entry per basket asked for, in the order asked.

nonAdditive.description: An instrument may be in several baskets, so the baskets cannot be added; true always.

minMembers.description: Fewest included instruments for a basket number.

ReportBenchmarksView.description: What holding each basket, and the benchmark index, would have done over one window (P8-07).

comparisons.description: Newest first. Empty is an ordinary answer.

limits.description: What always holds: in-sample, modelled fills, the same entries.

ReportComparisonsView.description: The stored comparisons of exits on identical entries (spec P8-10 part b). Choosing one names its member runs as the run set of a report; the report must then be split by exit (`lens=exit`).

firstDate.description: Earliest entry date; null without a trade.

lastDate.description: Latest exit date; null without a trade.

provisional.description: A contributing run is marked provisional.

runKeys.description: The runs behind the numbers, sorted.

runs.description: The same runs with their facts (the Data used panel).

defaultRunSet.description: The run set was not named by the caller: the newest run of each strategy and universe.

limits.description: The limits that always apply, as text.

unavailableInputs.description: Inputs a figure would need that do not exist, each with the reason.

duplicateTradesDropped.description: Identical repeated records of one trade in one run, counted once.

openAtEndLeftOut.description: Trades still open at the end of the data in the runs used, which no report counts; counted over the whole runs from their stored headers, before any date, symbol or basket filter of the report.

netBasisConfirmation.description: What the owner confirmed, for a net report; null for a gross one.

oneOf.description: Only on a report over a simulate-everything job (AU-14): that it is a training simulation, not evidence, how much of the job was read and what part of the range is locked; absent from every evidence report.

ReportEvidenceView.description:
The evidence block every report carries (P8-00 D1): the basis, the population, the date range, what is not available and why, the runs behind the numbers (the "Data used" panel) and the honest limits as fields. A screen renders these; none of this wording
is page prose.

selections.description: Newest first. Empty is an ordinary answer.

ReportExitSelectionsView.description: The stored out-of-sample exit choices (spec P8-10 part b, ADR 0054): which exit won each fold of a walk-forward, whether the choice is stable, and what the record itself says it is worth.

ReportHoldOutView.description: The hold-out row of a report (spec CF-06, AC12): `not_fixed`, `kept`, `used` or `reused`; the numbers only after the look was taken.

ReportKpisView.description: The headline figures of the out-of-sample evidence; a figure that is not finite is null.

nonAdditive.description: A trade is in more than one group.

ReportMaeMfeView.description: The excursions of a report for a lens, one entry per group, as counts in bins (never one point per trade), with the evidence of the report.

runs.description: Run keys (64 lower-case hex each); empty means the default set: the newest run of each strategy and universe.

lens.description: Dimensions to group by, in order: basket, instrument, strategy, timeframe, side, style, exit, month, weekday (regime and account are named and refused with the reason).

exit.description: Run exit labels to keep, separated by semicolons (a label such as `FIXED_RR{rr=2,x=3}` may hold a comma).

metric.description: The figure of a pivot (snake case, `expectancy_r` by default).

limit.description: Page size of the trade list, 1 to 1,000 (100 by default).

cursor.description: The cursor the previous page of the trade list returned.

purpose.description: `research` (default: the evidence reports) or `training` (a simulate-everything job: a training simulation, not evidence, AU-14).

simJob.description: The job a training report reads (a guid); the active-else-newest job when empty. Only with `purpose=training`.

ReportQueryInput.description:
The raw text of the one query model of the report endpoints (P8-00 D4): what the query string carries, before the whitelist. Lists are comma separated. There is deliberately no field for the basis confirmation: whether a report may be net is decided from the
owner's stored confirmation only, never from what a caller says.

ReportRegistrationView.description: The registration row of a report (spec CF-06, AC12): `registered` or `not_registered`, and the texts when registered.

ReportRunView.description: What was tested: the strategy version, the method, the window and the universe (spec P5-06).

ReportUploadForm.description:
The multipart form of the report preview and import, for the API contract only (the request is read by ReportUploads). `AccountId` is the account, `Files` the downloaded reports (one or more; CSV, XLS or XLSX). `Choices` is a JSON array of
`{name, holdingId | instrumentId | isin, remember}`: what scrip names of a transaction report mean. For the import also `Digests` (a JSON array with the preview's digest, or null, for each file in order), `Rebuild` (whether to rebuild the lots of
trade files, default true) and `AcceptOtherAccount` (a JSON array of the indexes, from 0, of the files to import although the report is for another client code).

ReportWarningView.description: A caution derived from the report's own numbers. It never changes the outcome.

ReportedCount.description: A count that is `ok` with its value, or `unavailable` with a reason word and no value: never 0 in the place of a non-value (P8-00 D3).

ReportedDate.description: A date that is `ok` with its value, or `unavailable` with a reason word.

ReportedShare.description: A share of 1 (or a plain measure in sessions) that is `ok` with its value, or `unavailable` with a reason word.

largestN.description: The most trades in any cell.

ReportsPhaseAnswerView.description: The What-works answer on the default set (spec P8-17).

report.description: The criteria, the answer, the timings and the limits.

ReportsPhaseCheckView.description: The P8 phase check as a read (spec P8-17).

headline.description: The headline; MET only on real evidence for every counted criterion.

criteria.description: Criteria 1 to 10 of P8-00, numbered as there.

answer.description: What the What-works view answers on the default set.

timings.description: The timed reads, cold and warm.

basketsWithTrades.description: Baskets with trades in the default set.

ReportsPhaseReportView.description: The body of the P8 phase check (spec P8-17).

operation.description: The operation id of the endpoint.

answerPath.description: On the answer path of the exit question.

coldMs.description: The first call; null when the read was refused.

warmMs.description: The second call; null when the read was refused.

ReportsPhaseTimingView.description: One timed read of the phase check (spec P8-17).

ResetEssentialRequest.description: The body of a reset: the owner's password, re-entered for THIS act.

ResolveBreakRequest.description: The owner's resolution of a break: `accept_broker` or `dismiss_foreign` (a foreign conflict only), an optional note of at most 300 characters and the password, checked afresh for this act.

ResolveInput.description: Pasted tickers, canonical symbols (`NSE:RELIANCE`) or ISINs, up to 5,000 entries.

ResolveResult.description:
The outcome of looking up a pasted list. `entries` counts the non-blank entries, `duplicates` those collapsed because an earlier entry
was the same text or named the same instrument. Entries that match nothing are never guessed: they are listed in `unmatched`.

ResolvedInstrument.description: An entry that named an instrument. `term` is the entry as typed (the first one when several name the same instrument); `tracked` = tracked now; `retired` = cannot be newly tracked.

ResultsCalendarView.description: The visible upcoming results meetings with an event session between `From` and `To` as known at `AsOf`, earliest first; `Truncated` when more than the cap exist. No file content and no estimate.

ResultsMeetingView.description: One visible upcoming results meeting: `Days` trading sessions from the India date of the question to its `EventSession` (the first session on or after `MeetingDate`); `IntimatedAt` is when the exchange published the row; `Revision` is 1 for the first row and 2 and up for reschedules.

ResumeServiceRequest.description: The optional body of `POST /api/services/{id}/resume`: the owner's password, typed again; needed only for a service with `resumeNeedsPassword` (LC-01).

ReturnsView.description: The profit/loss figures that every holding row, lot row and summary carries.

effectiveQuantity.description: The size after the owner's modification, or the allocated one.

canApprove.description: Whether this account's checklist allows approval without a confirmation.

checks.description: All checks in the fixed order, or empty when the plan stored no readable checklist.

ReviewAccountView.description: A ticket's checklist for one account.

outcome.description: pass, fail or unavailable, as recorded when the plan was built.

standing.description: passed, warned, needsconfirmation, confirmeddespite or refused: where it stands for approval.

ReviewCheckView.description: One check on the review screen.

notice.description: For an approval, string PlanWording.ApprovedForWatching; otherwise empty.

overriddenCodes.description: The checks approved despite, in check order (empty when none).

ignored.description: Confirmations (or parts of them) that covered nothing, each with the reason, so the owner sees that nothing was overridden by them.

state.description: value, provisional, insufficient, unavailable, not_evaluable or empty.

number.description: The number; null unless value or provisional.

reason.description: Why it is not a plain value.

n.description: How many items it rests on, when that is meaningful.

ReviewMetric.description: One figure of a review section on the wire and in the stored record: a state and, only for value and provisional, a number (P8-00 D3).

oneOf.description: A table, or null.

ReviewSection.description: One section of the weekly paper review (spec P10-03): lines of text, figures with their states, an optional table and the sentence of its limits that ends it.

rows.description: The rows; each has one cell per column.

ReviewTable.description: A small table of a review section (the closed trades of the week), as text cells.

checklistRecorded.description: False when the plan stored no readable checklist: the ticket cannot be approved.

canApprove.description: Whether the owner may approve it as it stands (checks all passed or warned).

needsConfirmation.description: The check codes per account that need the owner's confirmation to approve; empty when none.

approveAllEligible.description: Whether approve-all would approve it: primary, proposed, every check passed.

modification.description: The owner's size change, as stored, or null.

confirmedDespite.description: What the approval overrode (stored text), or null.

ReviewTicketView.description: One ticket on the review screen.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS act.

RevokeChargeSheetRequest.description: The body of a revocation: it withdraws the confirmation in force, whatever sheet that is.

RiskProfileInput.description: The values of a risk profile to create or to replace an existing one with. Every value is required.

RobustnessView.description: The robustness block of a result (spec P5-05, ADR 0062). It does not change the verdict; every part that cannot be computed is null or says why. `ByRegime` is the one-line text; since P6-02 `ByRegimeBuckets` and `ByRegimeUnavailable` carry the numbers (null in a result stored before it). Since SC-S1 (ADR 0222) `ByQuarter` (the quarters with a trade) and `MaxInstrumentShare` (the largest instrument's share of the total R, 1.0 when the total is not above 0) feed the readiness scorecard's row 10; both are null in a result stored before it, and nothing here changes the verdict. Since CF-03 part B (ADR 0228) `Pbo` (the probability of backtest overfitting of the sweep) and `VariantSeries` (the daily series it came from) are null in a result stored before it or with the PBO mode Off; they change the outcome only in the owner's Gate mode.

RolesInput.description: Roles to switch; a role that is left out stays as it is.

modelId.description: The champion it would demote to challenger (shadow).

trigger.description: `calibration` (the P6-09 calibration detector) or `band` (the P6-09 rolling band detector).

text.description: The detector's words, with the numbers.

cells.description: For the band trigger, the cells in alarm.

previousChampionId.description: The champion this model replaced, or null.

previousQualifies.description: Whether that model's latest evaluation satisfied the predicate without the switch when the proposal was written. Information only: it is never re-promoted automatically.

settingsHash.description: The SHA-256 of the thresholds that produced it.

proposedOn.description: The India date it was proposed.

decidedAt.description: When it was decided, or null.

autoSettingId.description: For an automatic decision, the row of the `ml.auto_rollback` switch in force; else null.

RollbackProposalView.description: One rollback proposal as the owner reads it.

RollbackProposalsView.description: The proposals and the switches beside them.

command.description: The verb or slice that would produce it.

RuleOutcomeView.description: The outcome metric of a rule.

universeKind.description: How the universe was chosen (instrumentlist or basket).

universeLabel.description: What the universe is, as stored.

windowStart.description: First India date of the run window.

windowEnd.description: Last India date of the run window.

costsSheetId.description: The charge sheet id; null for a gross run.

style.description: The style of the stored strategy; null when not recorded.

styleSource.description: Where the style comes from; null when not recorded.

exit.description: The exit candidate of the stored comparison the run belongs to; null when not recorded.

exitSource.description: Where the exit comes from; null when not recorded.

openAtEnd.description: Trades still open at the end of the data, never counted.

netPossible.description: A net report over this run is possible: it was costed with the very charge sheet, with the very rates, the owner confirmed.

inDefaultSet.description: The default run set takes this run.

defaultSetNote.description: Why the default set leaves the run out; null when it takes it.

RunListItemView.description: A stored run a report may use, with whether the default run set takes it and, if not, why.

RunSummary.description: The summary of a run: the verdict, the sets, and the sentence about the small sample. A run with one repeat is bool RunSummary.NonGating and can never be accepted.

universe.description: How the universe was chosen and what it is.

windowStart.description: First India date of the run window.

windowEnd.description: Last India date of the run window.

costsSheetId.description: The charge sheet id; null for a gross run.

style.description: The style label; null when not recorded.

exit.description: The exit label; null when not recorded.

closedTrades.description: Closed trades the run holds (before the filters of the query).

openAtEnd.description: Trades still open at the end of the data, left out of every report.

RunUsedView.description: One run in the "Data used" panel of a report (P8-00 D2): the run key, what it replayed, its window, whether it was costed and the labels a report took from it.

net.description: Whether a net report can be made.

defaultSetRule.description: How the default run set is chosen, as text.

RunsView.description: The stored runs a report may use, newest first, and whether net figures are possible (P8-06). With no stored run the list is empty, which is an ordinary answer.

SanityCheck.description: Bar sanity: low ≤ open and close ≤ high, prices positive and finite, volume not negative. `examples` holds the first few bad bars.

SchedulePreview.description: The dry run of a schedule: the findings (errors and warnings), the next three starts after now (empty when the schedule has errors or follows another service) and the schedule in words.

ScheduleSpec.description:
A Schedule as text: what the API sends and receives and what the database stores (JSON). `type` is daily · weekly · after · window · interval · continuous; times are
`HH:mm` India time; `days` are mon … sun; `weekday` is one of them; `after` is a service id. Fields that do not belong to the type are left out (null).

strategies.description: One line per strategy, weakest first.

ScorecardListView.description: The system card and the strategy table (spec CF-11).

id.description: The snapshot, which a gate decision can cite.

settingsHash.description: The settings hash it was computed with.

ScorecardPointView.description: One stored daily snapshot of a strategy's score (the trend).

producer.description: The slice or source that produces the input.

status.description: `pass`, `fail` or `unavailable`. Unavailable is never a pass.

threshold.description: The go threshold in words and numbers.

value.description: The figure it was judged on, or why it could not be.

ScorecardRowView.description: One row of the 15-row edge checklist as the API sends it.

ScorecardSummaryView.description: One line of the strategy table.

version.description: The strategy version the Lab results are read for; null when the strategy has none.

score.description: 0 to 100: the minimum of the applicable sub-scores, or 0 with a hard fail.

rawMinimum.description: The minimum before the hard fails.

notApplicable.description: What was left out because it does not apply.

weakestSubScore.description: The weakest sub-score by name; null when none.

whatWouldMoveIt.description: What would move the weakest sub-score; null when nothing is computed.

waiting.description: What the card is waiting for: the producers of the rows and sub-scores that are unavailable (unavailable is a fail, so this is the list of what to build or run).

notes.description: The honesty sentences: the basis of the figures and the interpretations.

enforce.description: Whether the owner's enforce switch is ON now.

settingsHash.description: The SHA-256 of the readiness settings.

history.description: The newest daily snapshots (the trend), newest first.

ScorecardView.description: The scorecard of one strategy version (spec CF-11 D1 to D4): the 15-row checklist, the six sub-scores, the hard fails, the label, the two gates and what would move the weakest link. Derived on every read from stored results; read only: it raises no size and places no order.

SecretStatusView.description: Whether one of the owner's Dhan secrets is stored (encrypted) and when it last changed. Name is the request field name ("apiKey", "apiSecret"). The value itself is never returned.

SecretsInput.description:
The Dhan API key and secret, write-only (app_id / app_secret). Surrounding spaces are
removed; the values are stored encrypted and never returned.

winner.description: The winning candidate; null when none qualified.

winnerTestScore.description: The winner's out-of-sample score as a state.

thin.description: The fold does not count toward the verdict.

SensitivityView.description: The parameter sensitivity (spec P5-05): the exit and timeframe every point used, the base and the parameters.

onTrack.description: The level the sum is reflected at; a label, never a pass.

cautionOdds.description: The evidence ratio at the caution boundary.

failureOdds.description: The evidence ratio at the failure boundary.

SequentialBoundariesView.description: The boundaries of the test, computed from the settings (never stored).

lowest.description: The lowest sum of the path.

lowestAtTrade.description: The 1-based trade of the lowest sum; 0 with no trade.

sigmaUsed.description: The sigma of the last step.

SequentialPathView.description: A short summary of the sum path (the whole path is not sent).

basis.description: What the R is: gross or net, and whose fills.

note.description: What the reader should know about the series: why there is nothing to test (no epoch, no graded trade), which session holds trades back, how many graded trades have no gross figure; null when there is nothing to say.

state.description: `monitoring`, `on_track`, `caution` or `failure`. None of them is a pass.

effectiveN.description: The trades over the design effect of their days.

firstCautionTrade.description: The 1-based number of the first trade at or below the caution boundary; null when never.

firstFailureTrade.description: The 1-based number of the first trade at or below the failure boundary; null when never.

heldBackTrades.description: Graded trades not in the series because an earlier session still has a candidate without a grade (the test runs only over the complete sessions from the start of the epoch, so a late grade can only add to the end and never rewrite a shown path); 0 for the behavioural series.

heldBackFromSession.description: The first session with a candidate still without a grade, where the series stops (it may never be graded: a replay can wait or fail for good); null when the series is complete.

SequentialSeriesView.description: One series run through the test.

epoch.description: The paper epoch both series are read for (the current one); null when there is none.

hasSeries.description: Whether any shadow edge candidate of the epoch exists in the scope (the endpoint answers 404 when not).

rhoIsPlaceholder.description: Whether it is the placeholder until CF-01 estimates it.

settingsHash.description: The SHA-256 of the settings that produced the figures.

edge.description: The edge series (graded shadow trades that count for edge); the primary reading.

behavioural.description: The P10 counted trades of the epoch, run through the same test, beside it.

statements.description: The honesty sentences: the model, the odds, the indifference point, the same-day discount, that the fixed gates decide.

line.description: One line for the report beside the P10 phase check.

SequentialStatusView.description: The sequential failure test (spec CF-09): the edge series of the shadow record with the P10 behavioural series beside it. A flag only.

ServiceIssueView.description: A finding of the schedule checks. `severity`: error (blocks saving) · warning. `field` is a dotted path like the request (schedule.time, retries, parameters.x); `relatedServiceId` names the other service of a finding that involves two.

ServiceList.description: Every service: the registered ones in screen order, then the read-only entries.

ServiceLiveView.description:
What a service that another process runs (the live feed) says about itself, from that process's heartbeat: `state` is its state word (connected · idle · connecting · reconnecting · closed · paused · no_token · token_refused · flapping ·
stopped · not_running when it reports nothing), `connected` whether it holds a connection, `subscribed` the instruments it carries, `lastTickAt` the time of the last price, `ticksPerSecond` its rate, `lastSeenAt` the
time of the heartbeat (null when it has never reported) and `summary` the one line the card shows.

ServiceNotice.description: A failure to tell the owner of (the bell). `id` is `service:failed:{serviceId}:{yyyy-MM-dd}` (the India date of the failed run): one notice per service per day, with the text and time of the latest failure. `kind` is service_failed; `severity` error.

ServiceRunPage.description: A page of runs, newest first. At most the latest int ServiceRunLimits.MaxShown runs of a service are shown; `total` counts those.

ServiceRunView.description:
One run (or attempt) of a service. `trigger`: scheduled · catch_up · after · manual. `status`: running · succeeded · failed · skipped; `queued` only in the answer to Run now for a service that another process runs (the live feed):
the request was accepted and the record does not exist yet (`id` is empty). `dataJobId` links the data job a run started.

ServiceScheduleInput.description:
The body of a schedule save or preview: everything the dialog sets, all of it required (a body that leaves a field out is a 400, so a missing switch is never read as "off"). `parameters` are the values by name
(those left out keep the schema's default); `revision` is the one read with the service (0 for a service that has no stored choices yet, also the default) and is only checked by a save.

ServiceStatus.description:
A background process by its heartbeat. `isAlive`: it reported within the last 60 seconds. `state`: what it says about itself (the feed: connected, idle, closed, paused, …; `stopped` in the last beat of a process that was told
to stop on purpose, which does not make the system unhealthy for ten minutes); null for a process that only says it is alive (the worker).

ServiceView.description:
A service on the Services screen (ADR 0018). `status`: healthy · running · failed (its latest run failed) · paused. `schedule` is the stored form (`scheduleWords` says it in words);
`allowedScheduleTypes` are the types the owner may choose; `isDefault` says the choices are the definition's defaults; `lastRun` is the latest run of any kind, `nextRun` the next
scheduled start (null when paused, when it follows another service, is always up or has no day ahead). `revision` is sent back with a save (0 until the first save or seed). A `readOnly`
entry is set elsewhere (`manageUrl`) and refuses writes. `live` is only given for a service that another process runs (the live feed): what its heartbeat says; its `status` is then derived from the stored row, the
latest run and that heartbeat (failed when it should be up and does not report).

ServicesTimeline.description: The trading-day timeline: market hours (null on a day without a session), the review cutoff, whether the date is a trading day and every enabled service's starts and bands.

SessionCompleteness.description: One trading session of the window as completeness sees it: the minutes the calendar expects, the ones stored, and whether a refetch already proved the day unfillable (`bar_gaps`).

csrfToken.description: Must be sent as `X-CSRF-Token` on every state-changing request.

idleTimeoutSeconds.description: The session ends after this long without a request.

expiresAt.description: Absolute end of the session, whatever the activity.

elevatedUntil.description: End of the step-up window (password re-entered); null when the session is not elevated right now.

SessionInfo.description: What the client needs to know about its session.

SessionLine.description: The per-session line (criterion 8). Runs read `readable`, `unreadable` or `missing`; string SessionLine.MedianState is `value` or `insufficient`.

SessionOutcomeView.description: How many sessions ended in an outcome (`pass`, `warn`, `fail`, `unavailable` with its reason).

SetAutoScopeRequest.description: The body of `PUT /api/auto/scope`: ids of baskets and of individual instruments; at least one in all.

SetBasketBenchmarkInput.description: The body of the choice of the basket benchmark (BK-06c): the id of a listed index of the instrument master.

SetOutcome.description: The outcome of one set: the state and, for a failure, the thresholds that did not hold, in words.

toStep.description: 1 (the first step) or a lower step than now. A raise by one step is refused with 409 live.gates_not_met unless every evidence gate passes (an unreadable gate is not a pass).

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS move (checked on every request; no step-up window is used).

SetRampStepRequest.description: The body of a ramp step move (spec P11-04). The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session.

SetState.description: How one set of the eval ended against its thresholds.

SetSummary.description: The summary of one set: its outcome, its rates with intervals, and the repeat figures (`pass@1` and `stability` where they apply).

SettingsCatalogItem.description: `Tier` is Essential, Advanced or Internal; `Safer` is higher, lower or none (none loosens both ways); `Source` is default, configuration, stored or section.

gaps.description: Gap sessions: the writer did not run before the open; never back-filled.

ShadowChainView.description: The chain of digests: the owner copies the last one outside the database, and `xd paper shadow verify` recomputes it.

gross.description: True when the figures are the gross R (before charges): no charge sheet, a sheet the owner has not confirmed, or a mix. The numbers, this flag and Basis always agree.

sheetIds.description: The charge sheets that charged any graded trade.

confirmed.description: Whether every such sheet is confirmed as the owner's.

ShadowCostView.description: What the R is net of, and whether it may be called net (P10-00 D5).

behavioural.description: The P10 counted trades of the newest epoch (the exit criterion's n).

edgeRaw.description: Graded shadow trades that count for edge.

edgeEffective.description: The effective n of the edge count.

candidates.description: Every stored candidate, set-aside ones included.

pending.description: Edge candidates with no stored grade yet.

notTriggered.description: Edge candidates graded as not triggered.

notGradable.description: Edge candidates graded as not gradable.

ShadowCountsView.description: The two counts side by side (criterion 10). The behavioural count is P10's own: the owner-approved, armed, primary, measured trades of the newest epoch. The edge count is the graded shadow trades that count for edge. They are never added.

rawN.description: Graded shadow trades that count for edge.

effectiveN.description: Raw n over the design effect of each day.

rhoIsPlaceholder.description: Whether it is the placeholder until CF-01 estimates it.

rhoNote.description: Says so when it is the placeholder, else null.

sessions.description: Sessions with at least one final grade: the sessions the pace is counted over (a session not graded yet does not lower the rate).

targetEffectiveN.description: The effective n the ETA aims at (60, as the paper programme).

etaSessions.description: Sessions still needed at the rate seen so far; null until 10 trades are graded.

etaNote.description: What the ETA is or why there is none.

ShadowEdgeView.description: The effective n of the edge count and the pace (criteria 8 and 9).

low90.description: The 5th percentile of the bootstrapped mean.

high90.description: The 95th percentile of the bootstrapped mean.

hitRate.description: The share of trades with R above 0.

ShadowGroupView.description: The graded edge trades of one group: n, mean R with a 90% interval and the hit rate. A figure is a state and a number only when it is a value.

available.description: Whether a shadow edge series exists in the current paper epoch (false: the other fields are null and Note says why).

note.description: Why there is no test yet; null when available.

edgeState.description: `monitoring`, `on_track`, `caution` or `failure` of the edge series; null when not available.

behaviouralState.description: The same for the P10 behavioural series beside it; null when not available.

line.description: The one report line (never a pass; the fixed P10 gates decide); null when not available.

ShadowSequentialView.description: The sequential failure test beside the shadow figures (spec CF-09 D7, ADR 0232): the same answer as `GET /api/paper/sequential` for the system scope, as a state and one line. A flag only, never a pass.

hasRows.description: Whether any shadow row is stored.

note.description: Says so when there are no rows (and why none is written while the switch is OFF); null otherwise.

statement.description: Always: modelled fills; no queue, no latency.

separateCount.description: Always: this is a separate count and the P10 exit criterion is untouched.

counts.description: The behavioural and edge counts side by side.

edge.description: The effective n and the pace.

groups.description: Overall (`all`), then primary, reserve and rejected.

costs.description: What the R is net of.

enabled.description: The new value of `paper.shadow.enabled`: ON lets the services shadow-write and shadow-grade work (they also start paused), OFF stops them.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS change, ON or OFF. It is checked on every request (a step-up window opened earlier does not count and is not used up or extended); wrong ones count toward the sign-in lockout.

acknowledgeGap.description: Accepts that every trading session missed since the chain's newest one becomes a gap row (never back-filled); needed to turn ON when more were missed than `Shadow:MaxResumeGapSessions`, else 409 `paper.shadow_gap`.

ShadowSwitchRequest.description: The body of the shadow-record switch. The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session.

ShadowSwitched.description: The answer of a switch change: the row and the new value.

mode.description: `ReportOnly` (the only mode offered), the mode when it was computed.

parentLevel.description: `star`, `strategy` or `system`: the group the cell is pulled toward, itself excluded.

parentMeanR.description: The mean R of that group without the cell.

tauSquared.description: The between-cell variance used, in R squared (never below the floor).

blend.description: How far, 0 to 1, from the parent toward the cell's own mean.

shrunkLowerR.description: The 5 % quantile of the posterior: ignores the uncertainty in the pooling parameters, so it is optimistic.

estimatedStrength.description: The Beta strength the shrunk win rate used.

shrunkWinRate.description: The win rate shrunk toward the group's with that strength (the P6-01 posterior stays on the row).

nUsed.description: The trades the precision rests on: the smaller of effective n and the weight n.

note.description: Remarks and the unavailable reason.

ShrinkageView.description:
The shrunk figures of a cell row (CF-02, ADR 0204), as the API shows them beside the raw ones: "an estimate of the past edge, pulled toward its group", not a forecast. Every figure is null when it could not be computed and string ShrinkageView.Note then
says `unavailable: <reason>`. It changes no other figure of the row.

SignFlipBaselineView.description: The sign-flip baseline: lenient (mean R against 0 given the trade sizes), not a re-run with random entries.

SimAllEstimate.description: The measured estimate (spec AU-12 non-functional): taken from the finished chunks once at least 1 % of the job (and one chunk) is done. An estimate, not a promise: throughput and storage per chunk were unverified until measured.

SimAllView.description: Progress of the job, read by the report view while it runs (AU-14, AU-15).

state.description: running, paused, completed, completed_with_failures or cancelled.

complete.description: The job is completed with every chunk done and none failed.

windowFrom.description: First date of the training window.

windowTo.description: Last date of the training window.

holdOutStart.description: First date of the locked hold-out block.

finishedAt.description: When it ended; null while active.

SimReportJobView.description: One job a training report can read: what it covers and how far it has got. A training simulation, not evidence.

nextCursor.description: The cursor of the next page; null on the last.

SimTrainingScore.description: The out-of-fold score of the model beside the best baseline (log loss and Brier score: lower is better).

SimTrainingView.description: The summary card of a training from the simulation (spec AU-13, acceptance 8).

SizingChangeView.description: One change of a sizing setting (or a budget) in the history.

SizingSettingsChangeBody.description: The owner's change of the sizing settings. A value left out stays as it is. The password is needed for every change. The actor is never taken from the body.

version.description: The newest settings row id (0 when none).

oneOf.description: The newest change with direction loosen.

SizingSettingsView.description: The sizing settings in force with their history (newest first, the latest 50). With no row everything is OFF. SizingChangeView? SizingSettingsView.LatestLoosening is the newest change that can only raise a suggested quantity or remove a limit, or null when none was ever made.

scaledTotalR.description: Total R with each trade's R times its scale.

unscaledMaxDrawdownR.description: Largest fall of the cumulative R from a peak (the start is a peak of 0), as stored.

drawdownChangePct.description: Change of the maximum drawdown in percent of the unscaled one (negative is lower); null when the unscaled one is 0.

totalChangePct.description: Change of the total R in percent of the unscaled one (negative is lower); null when the unscaled one is 0.

halves.description: The first and the second half of the trades in decision order.

summary.description: The words, for example `max drawdown 20 % lower, total R 40 % lower`.

SizingStudyResult.description: What the same stored trades would have returned with and without the scale (descriptive, before costs). Nothing here is a recommendation.

floorSource.description: `setting` (the stored floor) or `sensitivity` (one of 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 asked for).

withoutScale.description: Trades with no scale (too little history): taken at scale 1.

skippedNoNetR.description: Closed trades with no net R (a gross run): left out.

caveat.description: Descriptive, before costs, same trades; nothing here is a recommendation.

SizingStudyView.description: What the stored trades would have done with the down scale (read only, descriptive, before costs, same trades).

SkipTicketBody.description: The owner's skip, with an optional plain-text reason of at most 200 characters.

reason.description: In words, including the check codes that did not pass.

SkippedTicket.description: A ticket approve-all left alone, and why.

id.description: gate, throttle, meta, windows or correlation.

state.description: `empty` (no plan), `observed` (counts from plans) or `not_recorded` (the plan rows carry no code for this rule).

ranOn.description: Plans on which the rule ran: always null, a plan row does not prove a run (ADR 0111).

unavailableOn.description: Plans on which the rule was unavailable; null when not recorded.

partialOn.description: Plans on which some correlation pairs were not checked; null for the other rules.

moved.description: Candidates moved to reserve; null when not recorded.

notRecorded.description: Why a count is null; null when every count is known.

outcome.description: The effect of the rule: never a number today.

SmartRuleView.description: One rule. A count that the plan rows cannot give is null with the reason in NotRecorded, never zero.

state.description: `empty` when no plan is stored, else `observed`.

from.description: Earliest planned session; null without a plan.

to.description: Latest planned session; null without a plan.

flaggedPlans.description: Plans flagged for review (a rule removed half or more of its candidates).

limits.description: What the counts do not say.

SmartRulesView.description: The smart-rule evidence of P8-13: counts read from stored plan rows, and for every rule an outcome that is a named non-value until its input exists.

SnoozeAlertRequest.description: The body of a snooze: 15, 30 or 60.

SpikeCheck.description:
Spikes: a 1-minute move greater than `spikeMultiple` times the median move and greater than 1 %. One the next bar takes back (at least half) is a spike (a warning); one that is not
taken back is a `largeMove`, a real jump, only reported. `thresholdPercent` is the move a bar needed to count.

SpikeExample.description: A close-to-close move that was far above the median: `movePercent` is signed; `reversed` says the next bar took at least half of it back (a bad tick, not a real move).

StartDataJobRequest.description:
Starts a data job. `steps`: any of csv · dhan · aggregate · quality (default csv, dhan and aggregate; always run in that order); `forceCsv` loads CSV files again that were loaded already
and have not changed; `refetchGaps` makes the Dhan phase also retry the sessions it gave up on (status `unfillable`); `csvFiles` (at most 214 names from the CSV folder, only with the csv step) loads only
those files, still skipping the ones that are unchanged unless `forceCsv` — a name the folder does not have, or a list that is empty, is `data.invalid` (400).

StartDraftRequest.description: The body of `POST /api/assistant/strategy-drafts`: the owner's idea in plain text and, optionally, a basket the idea is about. The actor is never in it.

baselineRunKey.description: The stored run to change one thing of (64 lower-case hex).

oneOf.description: The one knob.

holdOutMonths.description: Months kept out of the judgement (0 to 120, default 6).

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS start and checked on every request (an earlier step-up window does not count and is not used up).

StartExperimentRequest.description: The body of a replay start. The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session.

StartHaltRequest.description: The owner's button. `scope` is system or account (then `accountId` is required); `level` is entries, cancel or exit_all (exit_all needs the step-up window). The actor is never taken from the body.

StartLabRunRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/lab/runs` (spec P5-02): a stored strategy version (the latest when `version` is omitted), the universe, the method (`quick`) and optionally the window (default: the last year of stored data), `slippage` (`default` or `conservative`: tiered floors, tier C excluded; CF-05) and `stress` (the cost stress block; default on for `robust`, off for `quick` and `full`), `nulls` (`false` leaves the chance and plateau block out of a `robust` run; default true) and `draws` (random-entry seeds, 200 to `Confidence:Nulls:MaxDraws`, default the configured 1000); either makes the run a labelled what-if (CF-07, ADR 0231).

StartLabRunUniverse.description: The universe of a posted run: exactly one of a basket and a list of symbols.

StartLabRunWindow.description: The window of a posted run, India dates, inclusive; both or neither.

StartQualityRunRequest.description: The body of "Run checks": the one instrument to check (null: every tracked instrument with bars).

StartRefreshRequest.description: Starts a refresh. `force` skips the "file unchanged" check.

runIds.description: The ids, in the order of the request.

pairId.description: The id the two runs of a pair share; null for one run.

trialNumber.description: How many replays have looked at this range, this one included (AC 12): "the 7th replay of this range".

elevatedUntil.description: End of the window in which sensitive actions are allowed.

StoredStrategy.description: A strategy family as the library lists it (spec P3-02d, D4): the id, the style copied from its first version, whether it is a built-in, when it was created, its latest version number and how many versions it has.

StoredToolCall.description: A stored tool call with its envelope (up to 64 KB), as the audit keeps it.

StrategyDetail.description: One family with the list of its versions (spec P5-01): no texts, those are read one version at a time.

StrategyIssue.description:
One located problem of a strategy text (spec P5-01): the model path, a stable code, a message, the severity (`error`, `warning`, `information`), the place of the field in the file (1-based; null when the path is not in the
file) and, for a problem of the rules language, the item-relative span (zero-based offset and length inside the condition text, ADR 0036).

StrategyValidation.description: The answer of validate (spec P5-01): whether the text has no error, its hash when it has none, what it declares and every problem. Invalid text is still an answer, not a failure.

StrategyVersionView.description: One stored version as the library shows it (spec P5-01): the text exactly as it was posted, its hash and lineage, and whether the text is free of errors under the rules of today.

sufficient.description: True with at least 30 trades; otherwise the figures below are null.

drawdownSign.description: -1, 0 or 1: the sign of the change of the maximum drawdown, scaled against unscaled (negative is a smaller drawdown).

totalSign.description: -1, 0 or 1: the sign of the change of the total R, scaled against unscaled.

StudyHalf.description: One half of the sizing study (a median split of the trades in decision order).

reading.description: The figure it was computed from, or why it could not be.

whatWouldMoveIt.description: The distance to the next anchor, computed from the anchors; null when already 100 or when it does not apply.

SubScoreView.description: One of the six sub-scores as the API sends it.

SubscribeAck.description:
The answer to `Subscribe`: how many instruments the connection now follows, whether the scope had more than the server follows per connection (1000 instruments, 1000 holding ids), in which case the rest get no pushes and the screen
keeps their prices from its reads, and `failed` when the server could not read the scope (the database is unavailable): the connection then follows nothing and the screen should subscribe again later. After a good answer the server sends the
current price of every followed instrument (one or more `pricesChanged` messages, within about a second), then only changes.

SuggestionDecisionView.description: The decision about a suggested dividend: `State` is `accepted` (with the `DividendId` created) or `dismissed`.

seen.description: Whether the owner marked it seen.

all.description: The whole population as one group.

SummaryView.description: The headline figures of the whole population (the KPIs of doc 13 section 2) with the evidence of the report. A population below the minimum sample has no figure, only the count and the reason.

SweepPointView.description: One run of the sweep (the base has an empty `Param`): the figures of a plain run of one exit, or the reason the engine refused it. In-sample.

SyncInput.description:
Body of "Sync now" (optional). Confirm: true applies an answer that would close all or most open holdings, which is otherwise refused with
`409 portfolio.confirmation_required` (the problem carries `listedHoldings`, `openHoldings` and `wouldClose`). With Confirm: true both
ExpectedOpenHoldings and ExpectedWouldClose are required (400 portfolio.invalid otherwise): the numbers the owner saw in the 409. If Dhan's answer differs
now, nothing is changed and the sync answers `409 portfolio.confirmation_stale` with the fresh numbers.

SyncRunView.description: A run of the holdings sync. Trigger "manual", "auto" or "import"; Status "running", "succeeded", "failed" or "skipped". Error is a short safe text.

SyncStatusView.description:
The refresh settings of an account and its latest run. Mode "off" or "daily"; NextRunAt is null when the mode is off. FirstImportDate is the date holdings
get when they are imported without a date of their own; HasHoldings is true once the account has any holding (the first import has happened). Running is
true while a sync or import of the account is in progress. The health (ADR 0027): `ConsecutiveFailedDays` are the days in a row whose last attempt failed (0 when the latest succeeded), `LastFailureReason` a code (`unavailable`, `rate_limited`,
`interrupted`, `rejected`, `token_expired`, `token_refused`, `not_connected`, `unexpected`; null while healthy), `Attempts` the failed attempts of the day of the latest failure and `RetryAt` when the next quiet retry is due (null when none is pending).

SystemBasketSettingsView.description: Which owner-act switches are on (BK-04): `fetchEnabled` = Baskets:System:Fetch:Enabled (index lists), `listFetchEnabled` = Baskets:System:Lists:FetchEnabled (the two NSE F&O files), `derivedEnabled` = Baskets:System:Derived:Enabled. The screen disables its buttons from these; the API stays the authority.

integrity.description: 100 when the integrity checks are clear, else 0 (an unreadable check is 0).

weightedMean.description: The weighted mean of the strategy scores.

equalWeights.description: True when the weights are equal because no plan risk share is available (labelled).

weakestStrategy.description: The strategy with the lowest score, or null when there is none.

reason.description: Why it is 0 when the cause is not a strategy (integrity, no strategy), else null.

share.description: Of the cell's losses; null when the cell has no loss. Tags overlap, shares do not add to 1.

lostR.description: Sum of the (negative) R of the losses carrying the tag; null when the analyzer did not compute it (never shown as 0).

TagCountView.description: A tag kind in a cell.

TickRecorderSwitched.description: The answer of a switch change: the row and the new value.

TickRecorderView.description:
The recorder as the owner sees it: the stored switch (`false` when never set), its history (newest first, the latest 50), the state word of the recorder's heartbeat (null when the feed host never reported) and the reasons it is not running now.
Nothing in it is tick data.

enabled.description: The new value of the owner's switch: ON allows the recorder to run (when the deployment flag and the service are on too), OFF stops it.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS change - ON or OFF. It is checked on every request (a step-up window opened earlier does not count and is not used up or extended); wrong ones count toward the sign-in lockout.

TickSwitchRequest.description: The body of the trade-tick recorder switch. The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session.

TicketChartLevels.description: The numbers of the ticket (P7-19) as the chart draws them; `Source` is `none` when the ticket carries none.

TicketChartRules.description: The text rules of the ticket.

resolution.description: exact, ambiguous or not_found (the symbol against the instrument master).

session.description: The last closed session of the plan: the levels' session, else the trading day before the plan date.

adjusted.description: True: adjusted by the corporate actions applied as of the session.

barCount.description: Bars returned (fewer than asked when the history is short; never padded).

levels.description: The ticket's numbers, a straight copy.

rules.description: The three rule texts and the validity.

TicketChartView.description: The daily context of one ticket (spec P8-14, ADR 0113): the last bars up to the planning session, the levels the ticket carries, and its rule texts. Read only; never a price after the session.

decision.description: approved, modified, rejected, lapsed or undecided; empty for a rejected candidate.

status.description: graded, not_triggered, not_gradable or pending (no grade stored yet).

TicketGradeView.description: One ticket with its grade as the API shows it.

stop.description: The stop level, or null when the stop has no number.

stopAnchor.description: "level" (a market level) or "close_of_d" (a distance from the close); null with no stop.

target.description: The target level of a fixed reward-to-risk exit, or null.

basis.description: The pinned sentence on what the numbers are.

TicketLevelsView.description: The indicative numbers of a ticket (spec P7-19, ADR 0109): rupees as of the close of the session, not tomorrow's price and not an order.

TicketTally.description: The confirm tickets of a session by outcome; double? TicketTally.MedianMinutes is the median from issue to tap and null (insufficient) below int TicketTally.MinForMedian tickets.

candidates.description: Candidates dated in the window, summed over the timeframes.

tierExcluded.description: Candidates left out because the tier was C or unavailable.

share.description: The share of the candidates left out; 0 when there were none.

TierExclusionView.description:
What conservative slippage left out of a Lab verdict (CF-05, ADR 0229): the candidates whose instrument was liquidity tier C or had no usable tier on the entry date have no trade, so the trades behind the verdict are the survivors of the filter and not a clean sample.
Present only on a run posted with `slippage: conservative`. Counts only; the candidates are those of the first (default) exit of every timeframe, which every exit candidate shares.

TimeframeCheck.description: The aggregates of one timeframe compared with the recomputed ones: `compared` buckets (stored or recomputed), `differences` among them.

TimeframeStat.description: A derived timeframe (`5m 10m 15m 30m 1h 1D 1W 1M`): the bars stored and the start of the newest one.

TimelineBand.description: A part of the day a service is up (`from`, `to` as `HH:mm`; a continuous service spans 00:00 to 24:00).

TimelineEntry.description:
What one enabled service does on the day. `kind`: mark (starts at the marks) · band (up over the band; an interval also gives `everyMinutes`). `followsServiceId` names the service a
run-after service waits for (its mark is the one of the service it follows, at the end of the chain).

TimelineMark.description: One start on the timeline: the India time as `HH:mm` and the instant.

ToolCallSummary.description: A tool call as the conversation read shows it under the answer (the stored envelope is read with `GET /api/assistant/tool-calls/{id}`).

ToolsStatusView.description: The state of the tool server as the status shows it: `ready`, `down` or `disabled` (the assistant is off, or no address and token are configured), how many tools it lists and the estimated tokens of their schemas.

TrackResult.description:
What a track call did (all counts are of distinct instruments): `added` never tracked before, `reactivated` tracked again after an
untrack, `alreadyTracked` nothing to do. `totalTracked` is the number tracked now.

TrackingInput.description: Instruments to track or untrack: 1 to 500 ids (duplicates are fine and count once).

TradeBadRow.description: A row that cannot be imported: the line of the file it starts on and why.

TradeBatchPage.description: One page of import batches, newest first.

TradeBatchView.description: One import of a file. `Status` is `imported` or `undone`; `ActiveTrades` counts its trades that are not voided and `Securities` the securities among them.

TradeCount.description: A number of securities and the number of trades of the file in them.

TradeFileSummary.description:
What was in the file. `Rows` are the data rows (empty lines do not count), `Parsed` the valid trade rows, `Duplicates` the valid rows that repeat a trade id of the file, `AlreadyImported` the trades of the file that are stored already
(and not voided), `NewTrades` the ones an import would store. `Bad` lists the first 200 bad rows (line, reason); `BadTotal` counts all of them.

TradeImportResult.description:
What an import did. `Batch` is null when the file had nothing new. `Imported` trades were stored, `AlreadyImported` were there already. With `Rebuilt` the lots of `HoldingsRebuilt` holdings were replaced
(`LotsReplaced` lots removed); `Report` is the preview the owner confirmed (statuses before the rebuild).

basketIds.description: The baskets the instrument was in when the run was made; empty when not recorded.

r.description: R on the basis of the report.

style.description: The run's style label; null when not recorded.

exit.description: The run's exit label; null when not recorded.

ordinal.description: The trade's position in its run: with the run key, the address of its replay (a closed trade, so open-at-end is false).

TradeLineView.description: One closed trade of a report: what it was, when, and its R on the basis of the report (gross or net).

TradeNotRebuilt.description: A holding (or security) that an undo could not rebuild: its `Symbol`, the `HoldingId` when it is a single holding, and the `Reason` — `ambiguous` or the mismatch (`negative_opening`, `sell_exceeds_open`, `fractional_after_adjustment`).

TradePage.description: One page of the trades of a holding, newest first, voided ones included.

TradePreviewReport.description:
The preview of a tradebook import — nothing is stored. `NotHeld`: securities the account does not hold now (their trades are stored by an import, not applied); `Unmatched`: those of them that are not even NSE shares or ETFs of the master list.
`Digest` fingerprints everything the preview shows (all securities, listed or not); an import with `rebuild` must send it back. `Securities` lists every security that is a holding or an NSE share/ETF of the
master list and at most int TradeCsvLimits.MaxListedUnmatched (200) of the unmatched ones; `SecuritiesTotal` counts all the securities of the file and `UnmatchedListed` the unmatched ones listed.

TradeRebuildView.description:
What rebuilding a holding's lots from its trades does. `Status`: `ok` (the lots would change), `unchanged`, `quantity_mismatch` (see `Reason`: `negative_opening`, `sell_exceeds_open`,
`fractional_after_adjustment`; nothing is applied), `no_holding`, `ambiguous`. `Q` is the broker's quantity, `Net` bought minus sold (today's shares). `HandDatedLotsReplaced` counts the lots whose date the owner chose
and `SyncLotsReplaced` the lots a sync added, among the `LotsBefore` lots that an `ok` rebuild replaces by `LotsAfter` lots. `RealisedPnl` is the profit of the pieces the trades sold. `AdjustedFor` counts the corporate
actions that changed a trade. `Digest` fingerprints this rebuild. `OpenCostAfter` is what the open lots cost after the rebuild (Σ open quantity × unit cost; also for `unchanged`), `BrokerCost` the broker's `Q × A`
and `CostDelta` their difference. The open quantities always add up to `Q`. With no sales in the file and an opening lot (the file does not explain the whole holding) `CostDelta` is 0, to within the rounding of the opening
lot's unit cost to 4 decimals (0.0001 × its quantity); with sales — or without an opening lot — the first-in first-out cost basis of the trades can differ from the broker's average-cost figure (brokers keep the average by the
weighted-average-cost method, a sale does not change it), which is shown, not hidden. `CostNote` is `opening_cost_fallback` when the trades cost more than the broker's average cost allows and the opening lot therefore costs the
average cost. The four are null unless the trades fit (`ok` or `unchanged`).

ordinal.description: The trade's place in the run.

openAtEnd.description: The trade was still open at the end of the data.

basis.description: gross, or net only when the owner confirmed the charge sheet the run was costed with.

legs.description: The fills, in the record's order; empty for a trade that entered and left in one fill each.

oneOf.description: The costing, or null for a gross run.

limits.description: What this picture does not show.

TradeReplayView.description: One stored simulated trade drawn on its own bars (P8-11): the trade, its legs and costing, the bars of its window at one timeframe with the coherence check, the decision-time features it has, and the evidence block (n = 1). Read only.

TradeSecurityView.description: A security of the file: its trades in the file and, when the account holds it, what the rebuild would do. `Matched` is true when it is a holding of the account or an NSE share or ETF of the master list.

TradeSkipped.description: Rows of the file that were left out because they are not NSE equity trades: how many, and how many for each reason (`derivatives`, `commodity`, `currency`, `bse`, `non_equity`).

TradeUndoResult.description: What undoing a batch did — or, with `DryRun`, would do (nothing is changed then; `Applied` is false). Undoing a batch again is a no-op (`AlreadyUndone`). Holdings whose lots came from trades are rebuilt from the remaining trades; `NotRebuilt` lists those that could not be (a mismatch, or ambiguous) and keep their lots, `HoldingsNotRebuilt` counts them. An undo cannot bring back lots the owner dated by hand or a sync added that an earlier rebuild replaced: the holding returns to one default-dated lot of the broker's quantity and cost (or to the shape of the remaining trades); `HandDatedLotsReplaced` and `SyncLotsReplaced` count what the rebuild removes (the lots of the holdings it rebuilds).

TradeUploadForm.description:
The multipart form of the trade preview and import, for the API contract only (the request is read by TradeUploads). `AccountId` is the account, `File` the tradebook (CSV), `Rebuild` and `Digest` are
for the import: whether to rebuild the lots (default true) and the digest of the preview, which is required with a rebuild.

TradeView.description: A trade. `Side` is `buy` or `sell`, `Source` is `csv` or `manual`. A voided trade does not count.

nextCursor.description: The cursor of the next page; null at the end.

TradesView.description: A page of the closed trades a report counts, in the order of the exits, with the evidence of the report. Never more than one page: the largest page is 1,000 trades.

TradingInput.description: The complete trading configuration (a replacement, not a patch); whether the role is on is changed with the roles. Mode is "paper" (default) or "manual_live"; CapitalSource is "fixed" (default) or "broker_funds"; Styles holds "intraday" and/or "swing"; allowed instruments: intraday EQ_MIS and FUT, swing buy EQ_CNC and FUT, swing sell FUT. Switching from paper to manual_live runs the live-ready gate (422 accounts.live_not_ready lists the failing items); the soft items need LiveConfirmReason, a typed reason of 1 to 300 characters recorded in the audit text.

TradingRoleView.description: Trading role. Mode is "paper" or "manual_live"; Profile is the name of the risk profile (null when none is chosen).

TradingSettingsView.description: Trading configuration. Mode is "paper" or "manual_live", CapitalSource is "fixed" or "broker_funds", Styles holds "intraday" and/or "swing"; instruments are EQ_MIS, EQ_CNC or FUT.

label.description: The sentence a screen shows beside every figure: a training simulation, not evidence.

jobState.description: running, paused, completed, completed_with_failures or cancelled.

complete.description: True only when the job is final, every chunk is done and none failed: the report then holds the whole job; false while it runs, after a failure and after a cancel.

chunksDone.description: Chunks finished (the ones this report reads).

chunksRunning.description: Chunks being run now (not read yet).

asOf.description: The instant of the read: a chunk finished after it is not in the figures.

windowFrom.description: First date of the job's training window.

windowTo.description: Last date of the job's training window.

holdOutStart.description: First date of the locked hold-out block: no number from it is read, ever.

rangeFrom.description: First entry date actually read; null when the asked range holds none of the window.

rangeTo.description: Last entry date actually read; null when the asked range holds none of the window.

rangeCut.description: The asked range reached past the window (into the hold-out block or beyond): the answer is the part before it.

locked.description: The sentence that says the rest is locked, when the asked range reached into the hold-out block; else null.

symbolsWithoutResults.description: Stocks asked for with no trade in the finished chunks within the range (not run yet, not tracked, or no signal); each is named, never silently dropped.

trainingRecord.description: The route of the training record of the job (what was trained from this simulation).

TrainingCompletenessView.description:
What a report over a simulate-everything job says about itself (spec AU-14, ADR 0243, ADR 0250): that it is a training simulation and not evidence, how much of the job it could read at the as-of instant, and what part of the asked range it could not answer.
Only finished chunks are read; while the job runs the figures change as chunks finish.

TransferInput.description: Instruments (1 to 500) to copy or move from one basket to another; `mode` = copy · move.

TransferResult.description:
What a transfer did. Only instruments that are members of the source are transferred: the others are `notInSource` (for a repeated move, the ones
moved before). `added` became members of the target, `alreadyInTarget` were there already, `removed` left the source (a move only),
`newlyTracked` of the added ones were not tracked and are now.

TrialsView.description:
The count of looks at a strategy family with its parts (spec CF-06, D3, AC12), as of the judgement. `HonestFactor` is the factor of the honest total; `FactorUsed` is the one the gates were tightened by, which is the old distinct-hash factor
until the owner turns `Confidence:Registration:CountInFactor` on (`HonestCountApplied`).

TurnAutoOnRequest.description: The body of `POST /api/auto/on`: the owner's password, typed again for this act.
